rows.anchor: Supersession | Relationship + Domain Event ... Retraction | Domain Event + State transition ... Contestation | Derived condition ... Reconciliation | Domain Event + Relationship
rows.statement: Records a fourth, hypothesis-only DDD classification of the four lifecycle relations: Supersession = Relationship + Domain Event ('A supersedes B' is a relation, not a state); Retraction = Domain Event + State transition (KnowledgeRetracted transitions EpistemicState to RETRACTED, described as an irreversible withdrawal); Contestation = Derived condition, explicitly NOT a state of the knowledge claim, existing only when an unresolved Challenge entity/relationship is present; Reconciliation = Domain Event + Relationship (ReconciliationOccurred establishes a resolved relation between conflicting claims without supersession). Maps Supersession to Nyaya's badha and Retraction to pramana-badha. Flags as UNRESOLVED whether these concepts belong in the core Kernel or a surrounding bounded context, noting 'the existing law does not require them.'

rows.anchor: Four documents, four incompatible classifications of the same four relations ... No two agree.
rows.statement: Tabulates that four separate source documents (S1-F010 at 11:16, S1-F014 at 11:36, S1-F015 at 11:43, this one at 12:36) each classify Supersession/Retraction/Contestation/Reconciliation differently, with no two agreeing (e.g. Supersession classified variously as state, relationship→state, relationship, and relationship+event); identifies this as the classification blocker named by S1-F013, now demonstrated across four attempts within 80 minutes; this pass uniquely adds that retraction is irreversible and that contestation leaves the claim's state unchanged; also notes that none of the four relations is law-mandated ('the existing law does not require them'), undercutting treating any as a Kernel member.

rows.anchor: Challenge — an entity/relationship whose unresolved presence constitutes contestation.
rows.statement: Introduces Challenge as a new candidate concept: an entity/relationship whose unresolved presence constitutes contestation; identified as the corpus-side analogue of a separate ledger's ConflictRecord, bearing on an unruled question about CONFLICTED-state/ConflictRecord cardinality; noted but not adjudicated.
missing: entity-vs-relationship determination

rows.anchor: The commitment is owned by the KnowledgeClaim aggregate — the structural locus of epistemic accountability. ... the aggregate bears the dharma (constitutional obligation)… It is the duty-bearer.
rows.statement: Records a dharma-lens argument placing ownership of the epistemic commitment on the KnowledgeClaim aggregate itself as duty-bearer (Nyaya: the aggregate is the pramatr/knower in this structural analogy); flagged as the corpus's only argument against splitting the aggregate, since every other force (S1-F016, S1-F017) runs toward decomposition; also flagged as conflicting with S1-F012's 'accountable epistemic object' framing and with any participant-relative account of knowledge, since here the aggregate itself, not a participant, is the knower.

rows.anchor: Confidence: high on quotations; medium-low evidential weight (model-generated, no citations, third pass over the same questions); several source sentences are truncated mid-clause.
rows.statement: Records an explicit evidential-weight caveat: high confidence on the quotations themselves but medium-low evidential weight because the source is model-generated, uncited, and a third pass over the same twelve questions (agreement across passes is not independent corroboration), with several source sentences truncated mid-clause.

rows.anchor: Call it: Candidate KnowledgeOS Relational-Temporal Model v0.1 ... Candidate formalization constructed — ready for adversarial validation.
rows.statement: Recommends renaming the critiqued document's status from 'Completed Core Definition' / 'Step 1 — Complete core formalization — Complete' to 'Candidate KnowledgeOS Relational-Temporal Model v0.1' / 'Candidate formalization constructed — ready for adversarial validation,' framing the document's value as having created a falsifiable model for Session 2 to attack.

rows.anchor: Yes, this critique is correct and necessary. ... This critique is methodologically sound and should be treated as a necessary correction before we proceed.
rows.statement: A second, independently-titled document ('Critical Analysis of the Candidate Formalization Critique') within the same file reviews the first critique point-by-point and endorses it in full ('strongly agree' on all 14 listed aspects: Zero Lens misuse, knows not yet Core, insufficient temporal distinction, reliability/confidence misplacement, Context overload, History over-claim, Transitions possibly derived, incorrect timestamp invariant, four-layer mixing, falsifiable-model framing, temporal-dimensions proposal, ValidAt/CurrentAt/CompleteRelativeTo distinction, RegimeResult∉KernelSubstrate); restates the path forward as a 7-item action list (treat as Candidate v0.1, apply adversarial validation, redefine temporal structure, remove probabilistic concepts from Core, decompose Context, test whether Transitions are derived, run the temporal experiment).

lineage_claims.target: the first-part critique in the same file
lineage_claims.quote: Yes, this critique is correct and necessary.

rows.anchor: DDD bounded context | Supports, but clarifies: the Kernel is the enforcement mechanism of the admission boundary, not the boundary itself
rows.statement: Records a systematic 14-lens vote (DDD bounded context, aggregate/invariant, domain-event/lifecycle, constitutional, evidence, epistemic-state, representation, semantic, determinism, provenance, team/Conway, assurance, essentialism, anti-god-aggregate) on the hypothesis 'Kernel = Admission Boundary', each lens answering what the Kernel is/must own/must exclude/which invariant requires the boundary/support-or-contradict; result: 13 lenses support, domain-event/lifecycle partially supports, and epistemic-state challenges outright, asking 'who owns epistemic state transitions after admission?'.

experiment.hypothesis: Kernel = Admission Boundary
experiment.setup: 14 independent lens framings each answer 5 fixed questions about the same hypothesis.
experiment.assumptions: Each lens must name the invariant it relies on and evidence it lacks.
experiment.inputs: The hypothesis 'Kernel = Admission Boundary'.
experiment.method: Apply 14 lenses independently, tabulate support/partial/challenge verdicts.
experiment.result: 13 support, 1 partially supports (domain-event/lifecycle), 1 challenges (epistemic-state).
experiment.interpretation: The two dissents share the same underlying objection: unresolved ownership of post-admission epistemic-state/lifecycle transitions.
experiment.limitations: Model-generated, uncited, does not address a same-day-morning falsification of a related hypothesis.
experiment.conclusion: Vote recorded as OPEN; no hypothesis adopted.

rows.anchor: the Kernel is the enforcement mechanism of the boundary, not the boundary itself. That is a third ontological category alongside S1-F009's boundary and S1-F012's domain space — and it contradicts F009 directly.
rows.statement: Identifies the DDD lens's characterization of Kernel-as-enforcement-mechanism-of-the-admission-boundary as a new, third ontological category for what the Kernel 'is', alongside S1-F009's 'boundary' and S1-F012's 'domain space' characterizations, and states it directly contradicts S1-F009.

rows.anchor: three independent arrivals at the lifecycle objection: F010 (11:16), F014's Admission vs Lifecycle contradiction (11:36), and two lenses here (22:50). This is the most durable objection in the corpus.
rows.statement: Notes the two dissenting lenses (lifecycle, epistemic-state) dissent for the same reason S1-F010 gave for demoting admission to 'first transition,' making this the third independent arrival at the lifecycle objection across the corpus (S1-F010 at 11:16, S1-F014 at 11:36, two lenses here at 22:50), naming it the most durable objection in the corpus.

rows.anchor: If the Kernel owned only admission, what would own supersession, contestation, and reconciliation? ... either: the Kernel must own the complete epistemic lifecycle ... or there is a separate Epistemic Context ... or the KnowledgeAggregate owns the lifecycle, and the Kernel is only the admission gate.
rows.statement: Records the document's own unresolved trilemma over who owns post-admission lifecycle transitions (supersession/contestation/reconciliation): either the Kernel owns the complete epistemic lifecycle, or a separate Epistemic Context owns lifecycle transitions, or the KnowledgeAggregate owns the lifecycle while the Kernel is only the admission gate; none of the three branches is selected, and the third splits Kernel from aggregate in a way S1-F014 §13 (aggregate is the boundary) forbids; 'Epistemic Context' as a separate bounded context is new to Session 1.
missing: selection among the three branches

rows.anchor: Confidence is assigned at admission (but derivation is unknown) ... Item 6 is labelled an established fact while conceding its mechanism is unknown ... precisely unruled W:C-11, and it is the second time a document has listed confidence as settled-yet-underivable (S1-F008 did the same).
rows.statement: Records ten items the document labels 'established facts' (single-gate admission, immutable identity assignment at admission, evidence admitted/preserved as references, justification preserved, epistemic state determined at admission, Confidence assigned at admission but derivation unknown, history recorded, constitutional evaluation at admission, semantic interpretation outside, mechanisms never become identity authority); flags item 6 (Confidence) as internally inconsistent — labelled a fact while conceding its derivation mechanism is unknown, the second document (after S1-F008) to do so, corresponding to unruled question W:C-11; notes item 10 as the clearest statement of the mechanism/authority prohibition, consistent with a separate ledger's obligation 4.

rows.anchor: Admission Boundary (most supported by F-1…F-5) · Epistemic Lifecycle Manager (most supported by lifecycle reasoning) · Constitutional Transition Engine (most supported by constitutional reasoning). ... Each hypothesis is supported by a different evidence base
rows.statement: Records three competing Kernel-identity hypotheses ranked by supporting evidence base (Admission Boundary supported by F-1..F-5; Epistemic Lifecycle Manager supported by lifecycle reasoning; Constitutional Transition Engine supported by constitutional reasoning), and observes each is supported by a distinct evidence base — reframing the disagreement as a question of which evidence base is authoritative rather than reasoning quality.

rows.anchor: this list re-asserts the aggregate the falsification de-defaulted; the document does not acknowledge that result, though it postdates it by ~10 hours.
rows.statement: Flags that this document's member-list re-asserts a KnowledgeAggregate-based ownership model that S1-F016/S1-F017's atomicity falsification (from earlier the same day) had already de-defaulted, without the document acknowledging that falsification despite postdating it by roughly ten hours.

rows.anchor: I would not yet: implement the proposed tuple; create KnowledgeAttribution; create a Knows aggregate; build the probabilistic regime; freeze the Kernel API; freeze the Core invariants. ... Try to prove that these things are necessary before we build them.
rows.statement: Recommends deliberately deferring implementation for now (no tuple implementation, no KnowledgeAttribution, no Knows aggregate, no probabilistic regime build, no frozen Kernel API/Core invariants), stating the discipline as 'try to prove that these things are necessary before we build them.'

rows.anchor: This is the most methodologically mature proposal we have seen. ... Yes, fully and enthusiastically.
rows.statement: A second, differently-titled document within the same file ('Critical Analysis of the Independent Researcher Proposal') reviews and fully endorses the temporal-epistemic-reconstruction proposal ('the most methodologically mature proposal we have seen'), restates its key formulas and the five-track structure, and adds a 6-item action list (run the temporal episode experiment; define the historical substrate; test reconstruction; apply multiple regimes; apply the remove-X test; determine Kernel membership).

lineage_claims.target: the first-part proposal in the same file
lineage_claims.quote: This is the most methodologically mature proposal we have seen.

rows.anchor: The subsequent DDD work falsified the assumption that conceptual relatedness alone establishes an aggregate or consistency boundary.
rows.statement: The ADR explicitly acknowledges the atomicity-falsification result (conceptual relatedness alone does not establish an aggregate/consistency boundary) as settled context, written roughly 30 minutes after S1-F019 re-asserted the aggregate hypothesis without acknowledging that same falsification — the corpus contains, within one evening, both a document that ignores the falsification and one that treats it as established.

rows.anchor: Status: PROPOSED · Decision Owners: HPA / Architecture Review Board · Decision Type: Architectural scope clarification ... It does not authorize implementation and does not reopen the existing KnowledgeOS Constitution.
rows.statement: Records the ADR's own declared standing: Status PROPOSED, owned by HPA/Architecture Review Board, an architectural scope clarification that does not authorize implementation and does not reopen the existing KnowledgeOS Constitution; flags that no adoption record for this ADR was found in the kernel/ corpus, and that a separate corpus census flags this document as one of three at highest risk of being misread as adopted architecture.
missing: adoption record

rows.anchor: Reading through all 26 lenses, I notice they naturally separate into four distinct architectural layers when viewed through DDD's separation-of-concerns lens.
rows.statement: Records a four-layer stratification of the 26-lens system: Layer 1 Observation Instruments ('How to See' — ask questions about the domain but don't decide; includes Vani/expression-meaning vigilance, Panini/anti-corruption-layer design, Karaka/domain-model discovery, Navya-Nyaya/relation modeling, Nyaya/invariant identification, Escher/identity-vs-value-object via 'what survives transformation?'); Layer 3 Decision layer (lenses that make architectural decisions about what belongs where, via a Lens->Architectural Decision->DDD Mechanism mapping); Layer 4 Mechanism Candidates ('How to Engineer'); Layer 2 is not captured in the read.
missing: Layer 2 contents

rows.anchor: the Entity/Value-Object question it calls decisive is the Escher lens's assigned role. So the corpus's most consequential question was produced by a Layer-1 instrument — an observation lens — not by a decision lens.
rows.statement: Observes that S1-F018's decisive Evidence Entity-vs-Value-Object question is exactly the Escher lens's assigned DDD role ('what survives transformation?'), meaning the corpus's most consequential question was produced by a Layer-1 observation instrument rather than a decision-layer lens.

rows.anchor: Revision · Supersession · Removal (without deletion of history)
rows.statement: Records a lifecycle sketch of Revision/Supersession/Removal-without-deletion-of-history; identifies 'removal without deletion of history' as a fifth formulation of the retraction question (after S1-F010, F014, F015, F018), the only one phrased as removal rather than retraction/withdrawal/contestation, bearing on an unruled question about historical-record deletion.
missing: whether removal is distinct from withdrawal/supersession or a synonym

rows.anchor: What is Knowledge? | Exact definition/theory ... What might survive all theories? | Candidate invariant ... Then Session 1 extracts. Session 2 attacks.
rows.statement: Proposes a uniform 18-question research-extraction table to apply to every book (what is Knowledge, what is not Knowledge/boundary, formal structure, subject/agent, sources, dynamics, normative criteria, completeness, uncertainty, temporal semantics, observation boundary, measurement, inference, hidden ontology, reconstruction requirements, limits, regime-specificity, candidate invariant), explicitly to avoid re-deriving 'what KnowledgeOS should be' from each source; assigns Session 1 to extract and Session 2 to attack, with independent mathematical research providing alternative models, only then asking what survives across theories.

rows.anchor: So I would extract this as a falsification question, not a new model. ... So this is not a new philosophical feature we should add. It is independent evidence that C-15 deserves serious adjudication. ... I would add this to our C-8/C-18/C-4 investigation, rather than create a new capability.
rows.statement: Identifies the project review's consistent method: for every philosophical challenge it states the challenge, converts it into a falsification question, routes it to an existing open workbook item (never a new capability/model), and explicitly refuses the architectural conclusion — described as the discipline the whole research programme has been trying to enforce, executed inside the corpus, and the strongest counter-evidence against reading Phase 2 as unconstrained philosophical accumulation.

rows.anchor: What exactly makes an evolving epistemic object the same Knowledge identity rather than a new Knowledge identity? ... it does not invalidate our 'identity assigned, never derived' principle. It asks whether we have sufficiently defined the conditions under which that assigned identity persists.
rows.statement: Records the strongest challenge: repeated challenges to the assumption that an identified knowledge object remains 'the same thing' because its identity persists, yielding the derived question 'what exactly makes an evolving epistemic object the same Knowledge identity rather than a new one?', routed to open item W:C-8; the same underlying question S1-F015 first posed as content-mutability; the disposition preserves the 'identity assigned, never derived' principle while opening only the conditions-of-persistence question.
missing: conditions under which assigned identity persists

rows.anchor: absence ≠ withdrawal — and describes withdrawal as potentially a process rather than merely an event. ... Is retraction a change in epistemic state, a relationship to prior knowledge, or a distinct historical act — and what must remain invariant across it?
rows.statement: Records a sixth retraction-question formulation (after S1-F010,F014,F015,F018,F021), the first to raise gradual (not merely discrete) transformation and to distinguish absence ≠ withdrawal as a new non-collapse adjacent to but distinct from the existing unknown≠absent≠false triad; disposed as independent evidence that C-15 deserves serious adjudication, not a new model.

rows.anchor: This is probably the most dangerous challenge to the current Kernel. … context may not merely modify knowledge; context may constitute what the knowledge is. ... Does the Kernel merely preserve context as evidence/metadata, or is some context constitutive of the identity of the KnowledgeAggregate itself?
rows.statement: Records the 'most dangerous challenge': context may be constitutive of what the knowledge is, not merely metadata/evidence about it, yielding the question whether the Kernel merely preserves context as evidence or whether some context constitutes the KnowledgeAggregate's identity; notes a separate ledger already makes context a constitutive prerequisite (absence yields pre-domain refusal, no KnowledgeId), so the real unanswered follow-on is what the identity of the context itself is; routed to W:C-8/W:C-18/W:C-4.
missing: identity of the context itself

rows.anchor: we must reject DeepSeek's architectural conclusion… we must not infer: therefore CONFLICTED should be replaced by perspective-relative truth. ... Does the Kernel distinguish semantic contradiction from perspectival disagreement before admitting something as a contradiction?
rows.statement: Records an explicit refusal of a perspectival-relativism conclusion (rejecting that CONFLICTED should be replaced by perspective-relative truth), converting it instead into the question of whether the Kernel must distinguish semantic contradiction from perspectival disagreement before admission — a pre-admission test rather than a state question, independently converging with a separate open item on ambiguity≠contradiction, reached here via Chinese philosophy rather than the ambiguity thread.

rows.anchor: Interesting question. But I would not put this inside the Kernel yet. ... The 'continuous transformation' claim should NOT be imported.
rows.statement: Records two further explicit refusals: the zhi/xing (knowing/acting) distinction is judged interesting but not admitted inside the Kernel yet, and the 'continuous transformation' claim is explicitly refused import — noted as pre-empting, on the same day, a later 'continuous change' position that appears elsewhere in the corpus's Knowledge-definition thread.

rows.anchor: authority is not simply a property of a source; it exists through role + relationship + context… but this must be handled very carefully.
rows.statement: Records the Confucian lens's argument that authority is relational (role+relationship+context) rather than an intrinsic property of a source, with an explicit caution to handle this carefully; routed to open item W:C-3 (authority adequacy); identified as a fourth independent arrival at relational (non-manufactured) authority, converging with S1-F002 and separate ledger entries KCON-013/KCON-018.

rows.anchor: It must not decide: what the final Knowledge definition is; what KnowledgeOS finally is; what the Kernel finally is; which Kernel model wins; whether something must ultimately be implemented. It may, however, record: IMPLEMENTATION CANDIDATE / POSSIBLE IMPLEMENTATION CANDIDATE / MECHANISM ONLY / RESEARCH ONLY / REJECTED-FALSIFIED / NOT YET DETERMINABLE
rows.statement: Defines the extraction session's authority boundary: it must not decide the final Knowledge/KnowledgeOS/Kernel definitions, which Kernel model wins, or implementation necessity, but may record research classifications (IMPLEMENTATION CANDIDATE, POSSIBLE IMPLEMENTATION CANDIDATE, MECHANISM ONLY, RESEARCH ONLY, REJECTED/FALSIFIED, NOT YET DETERMINABLE) — explicitly research classifications, not architecture decisions.

rows.anchor: S1-F016's falsification is an ativyāpti result ... S1-F008's too-small warning is an avyāpti claim ... S1-F018's Entity/VO dilemma is a candidate asambhava ... That three-way mapping is my inference, not the document's.
rows.statement: Applies the nine-family instrument retrospectively (as the extraction's own inference, not the source document's): S1-F016's atomicity falsification is read as an ativyapti result (over-inclusion), S1-F008's too-small warning as an avyapti claim (under-inclusion), and S1-F018's Entity/Value-Object dilemma as a candidate asambhava (a definition describing something that may not be able to exist); also reads Family 5 (Samsaya) as the methodological justification for S1-F013's refusal to collapse alternatives.

rows.anchor: the pratiyogi requirement is why that non-collapse holds — withdrawal has an agent and a prior assertion as its counter-correlate; absence need not.
rows.statement: Connects the absence typology's pratiyogi (counter-correlate) requirement to S1-F022's absence≠withdrawal non-collapse, explaining why it holds: withdrawal has an agent and a prior assertion as its counter-correlate, whereas absence need not.

rows.anchor: I would not tell Claude: 'Use Tarka Śāstra to redesign the Kernel.' ... use the Tarka-derived reasoning apparatus only as an independent falsification lens against the already-defined and adjudicated boundary. That preserves the architecture's sovereignty.
rows.statement: States an explicit sovereignty principle: Tarka-derived reasoning is registered as an instrument (TARKA-KERNEL-FALSIFICATION-001), not yet an architecture rule, to be used only as an independent falsification lens against an already-defined and adjudicated boundary — never to let Indian philosophy directly redesign the Kernel, which would 'contaminate the architecture'; identified as the third independent statement of research-must-not-become-architecture within one evening (after S1-F020, S1-F022).

rows.anchor: KnowledgeOS vs KnowledgeCore vs Kernel · altitude vs boundary · aggregate vs consistency boundary · capability vs invariant vs anti-capability · ambiguity vs contradiction · protect vs produce · knowledge vs wisdom. ... They are logical preconditions for valid reasoning about the architecture.
rows.statement: Records the source document's own defence of the corpus's vocabulary-distinction work, naming seven terminology collisions as logical preconditions for valid architectural reasoning rather than mere semantics; four were already independently recorded by this review (Kernel-four-ways, ambiguity/contradiction, capability-vs-invariant, aggregate-vs-consistency-boundary), and two are new to Session 1: altitude vs boundary, and protect vs produce.

rows.anchor: an admission procedure that reconstructs interpretation is circular — it uses the judgement it is meant to authorise. ... CONSISTENT — and this supplies the missing justification for that rule.
rows.statement: Argues the anti-reasoner constraint explains a repeatedly-observed but previously unexplained pattern — many documents insist the Kernel 'does not reason' or 'is not a semantic reasoner' — by supplying the reason: an admission procedure that reconstructs interpretation is circular, using the judgement it is meant to authorize; identifies this as consistent with, and supplying the missing justification for, a separate ledger's existing 'the kernel does not reason' rule and justification-path obligation.

rows.anchor: if the constraint holds, selection cannot be inside without circularity. That is an argument, not a ruling.
rows.statement: Argues the anti-reasoner constraint bears directly on whether interpretation-selection sits inside or outside the Kernel boundary: if the constraint holds, selection cannot be inside without circularity — explicitly framed as an argument, not a ruling.

rows.anchor: A question is not a claim, and a claim is not an answer merely because it was produced in response to a question. ... name/reference ≠ proposition/assertion
rows.statement: Records a provenance-of-response non-collapse new to Session 1 with no counterpart elsewhere in the corpus: a claim is not an answer merely because it was produced in response to a question; also records name/reference ≠ proposition/assertion and restates 'identity assigned, never derived.'
invariants: A claim is not an answer merely because it was produced in response to a question.

rows.anchor: Semantic retrieval must remain a candidate-generation mechanism, not an epistemic authority mechanism.
rows.statement: Records a same-shape constraint applied to a different mechanism (agent-memory/retrieval source): semantic retrieval must remain a candidate-generation mechanism, not an epistemic authority mechanism; identified as a second independent arrival at mechanism≠authority within the book block (after Audi's evidence≠adoption), consistent with a separate finding's exclusion of retrieval/search/ranking from the Kernel.
invariants: Semantic retrieval must remain a candidate-generation mechanism, not an epistemic authority mechanism.

rows.anchor: The books and lenses do not prove our Kernel architecture. What they have done is make the dangerous collapses visible: Representation ≠ meaning ≠ identity ... Evidence ≠ interpretation ≠ justification ≠ conclusion
rows.statement: Records the corpus's own negative verdict on its book/lens programme: the books do not prove the Kernel architecture; they make visible two dangerous collapse chains — Representation≠meaning≠identity, and Evidence≠interpretation≠justification≠conclusion (a four-stage chain finer than a separate ledger's two-way Evidence≠Authority/Inference≠Observation rows) — matching, by a different route (survey vs self-declaration), an independent finding's conclusion (take the distinction, refuse the ontology).

rows.anchor: NON-AUTHORITATIVE RESEARCH / BRAINSTORMING ... NON-AUTHORITATIVE RESEARCH MATERIAL TO ATTACK, NOT ARCHITECTURE TO ACCEPT ... Preserve distinctions until the domain itself proves that they may lawfully collapse.
rows.statement: Records the dossier's self-declared header status ('non-authoritative research/brainstorming', 'material to attack, not architecture to accept') and its governing rule 'preserve distinctions until the domain itself proves that they may lawfully collapse' — inverting the usual burden so collapse requires proof and distinction is the default; identified as the fourth statement of the research≠architecture discipline within roughly 26 hours, and the methodological complement to the 'boring Kernel' principle (minimal Kernel, maximal distinctions).
invariants: Preserve distinctions until the domain itself proves that they may lawfully collapse.

rows.anchor: Do not ask only 'What does this book teach us?' Ask 'What would this book make us stop believing about KnowledgeOS?'
rows.statement: Records a research-extraction-prompt inversion built into intake rather than applied afterward: ask what a book would make us stop believing about KnowledgeOS, not merely what it teaches; notes the corpus thus has falsification instruments at both ends (intake-time via this inversion, and post-ruling via S1-F023's nine-family instrument), though the post-ruling instrument was never actually run.

rows.anchor: Knowledge should preserve the structure and reasoning required to reconstruct a solution, rather than merely preserve the solution itself. ... A candidate that fits the current observations is not necessarily uniquely established
rows.statement: Records Logitica's contribution: knowledge should preserve the structure and reasoning required to reconstruct a solution, not merely the solution itself; and that a candidate fitting current observations is not necessarily uniquely established (different explanations can be compatible with the same observational boundary) — read as underdetermination stated as an admission problem, independent support for the plural-interpretation question from a problem-solving source rather than a philosophical one.

rows.anchor: The object being known may itself be dynamic, relational, emergent, and only pragmatically bounded ... a deliberately selected boundary for a particular model, language, responsibility and interaction regime.
rows.statement: Records Philosophy of Complex Systems's contribution: the object being known may itself be dynamic, relational, emergent, and only pragmatically bounded, with a bounded context read as a deliberately selected boundary for a particular model/language/responsibility/interaction regime; read as the corpus's strongest challenge to a stable referent — if the known object is only pragmatically bounded, identity-of-what becomes unstable, a third independent route (after S1-F015, S1-F022) to the identity-through-change question.

rows.anchor: S1-F008's nine capabilities were asserted as "existing law" with the F-1…F-5 record absent; S1-F019 listed Confidence as an "established fact" while conceding its derivation is unknown; S1-F013's three candidate models were proposed with evidence declared insufficient. ... That mapping is my inference, not the documents'.
rows.statement: Applies the evidential-bridge requirement (as its own inference, not the source documents') self-indictingly to three earlier findings: S1-F008's nine capabilities asserted as 'existing law' without the underlying record; S1-F019's Confidence listed as an established fact while its derivation is conceded unknown; S1-F013's three candidate models proposed with evidence declared insufficient — each a high-value architectural claim lacking an identifiable evidential bridge; also identifies this constraint family as the generalization of two existing invariant rows (canonical-form equality is a similarity claim, not an identity determination; probability≠truth, canonicalization≠authority, low entropy≠certainty).

rows.anchor: Negative and superseded knowledge are still knowledge about the evolution of the knowledge state.
rows.statement: Records a Nyaya-Vaisesika (Indian Logic and Atomism) claim: negative and superseded knowledge are still knowledge about the evolution of the knowledge state — an eighth angle on retraction (after F010,F014,F015,F018,F021,F022,F023), the first that keeps the retracted content inside the knowledge set, changing what it is knowledge of rather than whether it is knowledge; also carries vyapti (invariable concomitance) already recorded as part of the nine-family Tarka instrument.

rows.anchor: Formalize the epistemic architecture we have extracted, then test it against technical/DDD/architecture scenarios. ... Can the KnowledgeOS epistemic model actually represent real engineering knowledge without losing its important distinctions?
rows.statement: Records a research-direction document recommending 'formalize first, then test against scenarios,' noted as ordering the same two activities (falsification and formalization) oppositely to S1-F026's 'falsify first, especially scenario-based DDD analysis' stated only 19 minutes earlier — recorded as an unresolved ordering conflict; the accompanying test question ('can the model represent real engineering knowledge without losing its important distinctions?') is identified as the sharpest acceptance criterion in the corpus, a representability test complementing S1-F026's preserve-distinctions rule.

rows.anchor: the eight competing formulations (S1-F009…F019) argue about contents … while presenting themselves as rival answers about the Kernel as such. And S1-F016's falsification attacked contents co-location, not extent.
rows.statement: Reframes eight prior findings (S1-F009..F019) as mostly contents disputes presented as rival extent claims; re-reads S1-F016's atomicity falsification as attacking contents co-location, not extent, which rescues that result from being over-read; identifies S1-F020's ADR as the only research document that separates the altitudes (KnowledgeOS ⊃ KnowledgeCore ⊃ Kernel), though without using extent/contents vocabulary; notes the corpus's four-way 'Kernel' vocabulary collision (S1-F020) does real damage precisely where an extent-answering document and a contents-answering document look like rivals and are not.

rows.anchor: None of the six Wave 1 items can change the extent. ... The first wave that can change extent is Wave 2: F-CM-1b (does selection sit inside?), C-3, C-10 (capability scope) — then C-4 in Wave 3 (what crosses the gate).
rows.statement: Records the formal track's claim that none of the six Wave-1 adjudication items (Wisdom, C-15, C-17, F-CM-1a, C-18, C-14) can change the Kernel's extent — each repairs surrounding law/vocabulary/ACL instead — so Wave 1 can be ruled with zero risk to the boundary's extent; the first extent-changing items are Wave 2 (F-CM-1b: does selection sit inside; C-3; C-10 capability scope), then C-4 in Wave 3 (what crosses the gate); notes S1-F025's anti-reasoner constraint bears directly on F-CM-1b (selection inside implies circularity), so the research corpus's sharpest constraint lands on the first extent-changing question — recorded as a convergence, not an endorsement.

rows.anchor: Whatever retraction is, it passes the same gate ... C-18 has the most no-amendment options of any Wave 1 item — four ... C-15 has the fewest. Its two leading options both require amendment…
rows.statement: Records the formal track's containment claim 'whatever retraction is, it passes the same gate' (a claim about W:C-15 that none of the corpus's eight retraction angles across S1-F010,F014,F015,F018,F021,F022,F023,F027 itself makes), and an amendment-pressure ordering where C-18 has the most no-amendment options (four) and C-15 the fewest (its two leading options both require amendment); notes this is a genuine cross-track convergence — the item the research corpus cannot settle (W:C-15) is the item the formal track finds hardest to rule without amendment — recorded, not adjudicated or endorsed.

rows.anchor: If evidence does not support a sufficiently safe decision, abstention is a valid result. ... we can't tell from the data available.
rows.statement: Records abstention as a first-class output constraint drawn from Freedman's Statistical Models and Causal Inference ('we can't tell from the data available'), described as epistemic discipline preventing a system from turning models/correlations/assumptions/fluent explanations into unjustified knowledge; a third independent arrival at abstention as a required capability (after Audi's evidence≠adoption and a separate ledger's declared-insufficiency obligation), adding a stronger decision-safety framing: abstention is licensed by insufficient grounds for a SUFFICIENTLY SAFE decision, making the threshold consequence-relative rather than merely grounds-relative.
invariants: If evidence does not support a sufficiently safe decision, abstention is a valid result.

rows.anchor: fluent explanations ... names the failure where articulacy substitutes for warrant
rows.statement: Identifies Freedman's phrase 'fluent explanations' as naming the failure mode where articulacy substitutes for warrant, converging independently with S1-F027's evidential-bridge requirement.

rows.anchor: How should a governed domain system mutate and preserve state? ... How should a knowledge system discover, assemble, rank, contextualize, evaluate, and operationalize information for an AI system?
rows.statement: Records RAG positioned as a controlled knowledge-access/projection layer, not the knowledge model itself, a third arrival at mechanism≠authority (after Audi's evidence≠adoption and a retrieval claim in S1-F025), consistent with a separate finding's exclusion of retrieval/search/ranking from the Kernel.

rows.anchor: AI may recommend, analyze, classify and propose; authority remains explicitly assigned. ... Fairness, Explanatory Ability, Auditability and Safety (FEAS)
rows.statement: Records a sixth arrival in the authority family and its cleanest verb-level statement: AI may recommend/analyze/classify/propose, but authority remains explicitly assigned — assign is not among the permitted verbs; also records the FEAS (Fairness, Explanatory Ability, Auditability, Safety) assurance framework name, research-only, no placement claimed.
invariants: AI may recommend, analyze, classify and propose; authority remains explicitly assigned.

rows.anchor: How knowledge should be justified versus How a system can reliably represent, mutate, persist, validate, publish, and project that knowledge. ... the source of the CQRS sense of "projection"
rows.statement: Identifies Architecture Patterns with Python (4,186 lines) as the corpus's only implementation-altitude document, contributing a technical pattern vocabulary (repository, unit of work, aggregate, domain events, message bus, CQRS) and traces the CQRS sense of 'projection' — previously recorded as a vocabulary collision with epistemic projection — to this single document, making the five senses of 'projection' one imported technical term plus four research senses rather than five independent confusions; classified as implementation evidence for patterns, explicitly not a Kernel model.
invariants: A mathematical or technical model is not automatically a Kernel model.

rows.anchor: evidence acquisition is its own domain ... the domain admits evidence, but does not acquire it.
rows.statement: Records a design proposal that evidence acquisition (create/acquire/select/preserve/qualify) is its own domain, directly tensioning with S1-F011's exclusion of Evidence Acquisition as a mechanism ('the domain admits evidence, but does not acquire it'); notes this tension is partly dissolvable by S1-F028's extent/contents distinction (acquisition could be its own bounded context, outside the Kernel's extent), though neither document makes that move; recorded as unresolved.
missing: resolution of the acquisition-as-domain-vs-mechanism tension

rows.anchor: A mechanism for distinguishing 'the data show a relationship' from 'the evidence supports that changing X would change Y.'
rows.statement: Records a new non-collapse from Hernan & Robins' Causal Inference: What If — observed association ≠ intervention warrant — as the causal analogue of S1-F027's inference-licensing family (another prohibited inference, from correlation to actionability); notes its practical bite is that a claim may be well-evidenced as association yet still not license action, a distinction the corpus's confidence discussions never separate.

rows.anchor: Do not automatically turn every noun into a domain object.
rows.statement: Records the corpus's most compact statement of its own recurring failure mode: 'do not automatically turn every noun into a domain object,' identified as the same discipline as the atomicity-not-relatedness criterion and the ativyapti (over-inclusion) test, but stated as a modelling-time rule rather than a review-time test.
invariants: Do not automatically turn every noun into a domain object.

rows.anchor: No new architecture without an activation event. ... Deterministic does not mean demanded.
rows.statement: Extracts two governance rules from a misfiled architecture-baseline reconstruction document: 'no new architecture without an activation event' and 'deterministic does not mean demanded' — the latter offered as a candidate third position on the corpus's determinism contradiction (whether the Kernel is a deterministic runtime): determinism may be available without being required; explicitly flagged as not applied and not adjudicated, since the source document is a baseline, not a ruling.
invariants: No new architecture without an activation event.

rows.anchor: do NOT accept the KnowledgeAggregate hypothesis yet. Treat your previous result as a hypothesis-generating round, not an architectural decision. ... For every conclusion classify it as: ESTABLISHED / STRONGLY SUPPORTED / HYPOTHESIS / UNRESOLVED / FALSIFIED.
rows.statement: Records the first corpus document where the project commissions a falsification of its own leading result with a required five-value verdict vocabulary (ESTABLISHED/STRONGLY SUPPORTED/HYPOTHESIS/UNRESOLVED/FALSIFIED), sharpening the question to 'what is the smallest domain fact whose integrity KnowledgeOS must protect, and what exact invariant requires that fact to be transactionally consistent?', separating semantic relatedness from transactional atomicity and instructing an attempt to falsify.

experiment.hypothesis: The KnowledgeAggregate (six-part member set) is the smallest transactional consistency boundary.
experiment.setup: Score each candidate member pair on semantic relatedness and on transactional-atomicity requirement separately.
experiment.assumptions: Aggregate validity requires atomicity, not mere relatedness (KCON-012).
experiment.inputs: Six candidate members: Identity, Evidence References, Justification, Epistemic State, Confidence, History.
experiment.method: Pair-by-pair scoring of relatedness (Strong/Moderate) vs atomicity (WEAK/co-location required).
experiment.result: All five scored pairs: Strong relatedness, WEAK atomicity — none requires co-location.
experiment.interpretation: The six-part aggregate is held together by relatedness, not atomicity, which is precisely the failure the atomicity-not-relatedness criterion predicts.
experiment.limitations: Three of the five verdicts depend on premises (state-is-derived, identity-assigned-before-justification, history-as-separable-event-sequence) themselves contested elsewhere in the corpus.
experiment.conclusion: KnowledgeAggregate hypothesis FALSIFIED as a single consistency boundary; recorded, not adopted.

rows.anchor: The research was right about the invariants, but the earlier KnowledgeAggregate was too large as a literal DDD aggregate. ... the invariants survive, the aggregate does not.
rows.statement: Records a later, independent project-voiced restatement (added during a continuous corpus pass) that splits invariants from the aggregate: the invariants survive, the aggregate does not — meaning the falsification targets contents co-location, not the invariant set, aligning exactly with S1-F028's extent/contents distinction; a further synthesis document independently states 'do not implement the earlier God KnowledgeAggregate literally' (proposal weight only, census-flagged as a document at high risk of being read as architecture).

lineage_claims.quote: The research was right about the invariants, but the earlier KnowledgeAggregate was too large as a literal DDD aggregate.

rows.anchor: Arrival count for the atomicity-not-relatedness finding (KCON-012): now six ... the most repeatedly and independently reached result in the entire corpus, and the only one restated by both project and model voices across both phases.
rows.statement: Records that the atomicity-not-relatedness finding (KCON-012) now has six independent arrivals across the corpus (Phase 1 origin, an initial DDD critique, this falsification, a phase consolidation, and two later documents), the most repeatedly and independently reached result in the entire corpus and the only one restated by both project-voiced and model-voiced documents across both phases; the finding's confidence rises to high while the falsification's underlying premises remain contested.

rows.anchor: Axis 2 (contextual identity) is the same claim S1-F022 recorded as "the most dangerous challenge" (context may constitute knowledge) arriving at identity rather than at knowledge. ... Axis 1 (transformational identity) is the third route to the question first recorded at S1-F015 ... Fourth arrival, and the only one that denies fixity outright
rows.statement: Connects axis 2 to S1-F022's 'most dangerous challenge' (context may be constitutive of knowledge) now relocated to identity, noting a separate ledger already makes context a constitutive prerequisite of identity, so what's new is the claim that identity IS a relation between entity and context rather than a property context merely enables; connects axis 1 to a fourth arrival at the identity-through-change question (after S1-F015 content-mutability, S1-F022 identity≠continuity, S1-F026 pragmatically-bounded-object), the only one denying fixity outright rather than asking for persistence conditions.

rows.anchor: This research does not answer this question. Instead, it exposes the challenge and asks the question for architectural investigation. ... Challenge the architecture; do not become its architect.
rows.statement: Records the document's explicit refusal to answer its own three-axis identity question, built into its own declared mode ('Challenge the architecture; do not become its architect') rather than applied afterward — the cleanest instance of the research-must-not-become-architecture discipline in the corpus; consequently the finding to record is a question with three axes, not a rival identity model.

rows.anchor: S1-F016 ... demoted identity to "an administrative concern"; ziran says identity is too fundamental to be assigned. Two attacks on the same invariant from opposite sides, neither reconciled.
rows.statement: Identifies that S1-F016 and this ziran challenge attack the identity invariant from opposite directions — S1-F016 demotes identity to 'an administrative concern' (too minor to require protection), ziran argues identity is too fundamental to be captured by forced assignment (too significant to be merely administered) — two attacks on the same invariant from opposite sides, neither reconciled.

rows.anchor: What happens when a system encounters something it did not know before? ... Contradiction is not an error to hide. It is an epistemically valuable event.
rows.statement: Records Chivers' (Everything Is Predictable) claim that contradiction is not an error to hide but an epistemically valuable event, identified as independent external support for a separate ledger's existing rule that contradiction is a state, not an error; also records the surprise/novelty framing question 'what happens when a system encounters something it did not know before?' as stating the surprise problem the corpus otherwise handles only as admission.
invariants: Contradiction is a state, not an error.

rows.anchor: Do not implement the earlier 'God KnowledgeAggregate' literally. ... Absence of knowledge must not be represented as falsehood.
rows.statement: Records a synthesis document independently restating 'absence of knowledge must not be represented as falsehood' (matching a separate ledger's unknown≠absent≠false rule) and a further arrival at the god-object refusal ('do not implement the earlier God KnowledgeAggregate literally'), flagging the source document as census-flagged as one of three at highest risk of being read as adopted architecture, so its disposition carries proposal weight only.
invariants: Absence of knowledge must not be represented as falsehood.

rows.anchor: Bayesian inference should be a supporting epistemic mechanism, not the KnowledgeOS Kernel itself. ... There is no single 'Knowledge Score' ... This book substantially strengthens the Kernel, but it also tells us what must remain outside the Kernel.
rows.statement: Records the third and fourth independent arrivals at the regime-not-ontology verdict (after an earlier Phase-1 statement and a Fagin resolution): Rescorla (Bayesian inference is a supporting mechanism, not the Kernel), a mathematical-modelling source ('there is no single Knowledge Score,' KnowledgeOS needs multiple mathematical representations), and Shieber (this book strengthens the Kernel but also shows what must stay outside it); identifies this as the strongest convergence in the corpus — six different formalisms (Bayesian inference, mathematical modelling, measure theory, possible worlds, information theory, HSMM) reaching the same placement — and 'no single Knowledge Score' as foreclosing scalar quantification at the level of type, not accuracy.
invariants: There is no single Knowledge Score.

rows.anchor: Inquiry is not the same thing as Knowledge. ... KnowledgeOS should not become a decision engine merely because knowledge influences decisions.
rows.statement: Records two new distinctions from Ammerman & Singer: Inquiry ≠ Knowledge, completing a chain separating Question/Inquiry from Knowledge; and a scope-creep prohibition that influence does not confer membership (KnowledgeOS should not become a decision engine merely because knowledge influences decisions), identified as a second arrival at the influence-is-not-membership principle (after S1-F020's consumption rule, here applied to decisions rather than contexts).
invariants: Influence does not confer Kernel membership.

rows.anchor: Was this input allowed to participate? ... a participation/authorisation question distinct from sufficiency — it asks about standing, not strength.
rows.statement: Records Shieber's one-line admission test 'was this input allowed to participate?' as a standing question distinct from sufficiency, adjacent to but not reducible to an unruled authority-adequacy item or S1-F029's evidence-role constraint.

rows.anchor: Semantic grounding must be attached to epistemic quantities. ... a bare number cannot cross a boundary.
rows.statement: Records Rescorla's requirement that semantic grounding must attach to epistemic quantities, read as the constructive counterpart to a separate finding that semantic entropy is knowledge-base-relative and to the existing low-entropy≠certainty rule: a bare number cannot cross a boundary ungrounded; the most implementable item in the block, bearing on unruled Confidence-derivability by requiring whatever Confidence is to carry its grounding wherever it travels.
invariants: Semantic grounding must be attached to epistemic quantities; a bare number may not cross a boundary ungrounded.

rows.anchor: Knowledge is not a possession — it is a relationship. A Kernel must model that relationship, not just the proposition.
rows.statement: Records a synthesis document's restatement of the corpus's already-established relationship genus for Knowledge (Knowledge is a relationship, not a possession), explicitly noted as recurrence within a synthesis summarizing seven prior works rather than an independent new arrival, so no confidence increase is warranted.

rows.anchor: cost arguments reward more Kernel content, invariant arguments reward less. ... a tension in justification type, not a contradiction in content.
rows.statement: Identifies a tension between the economic (cost-saving) justification for a Kernel and the corpus's constitutional (invariant-protection) framing: the two license opposite design pressures (cost arguments reward more Kernel content; invariant arguments reward less), recorded as a tension in justification type rather than a contradiction in content, since both could be true simultaneously.

rows.anchor: Zero asks: 'What happens when a prerequisite is missing?' ... Leonardo asks: 'Have we understood the whole relevant context before we decide?' ... Context present ≠ context understood
rows.statement: Records two lens questions in their most operational form in the corpus: Zero ('what happens when a prerequisite is missing?', consistent with an existing constitutive-prerequisite-absence rule) and Leonardo ('have we understood the whole relevant context before we decide?', with no existing counterpart, since the current law requires context to be present but not sufficient); proposes 'context present ≠ context understood' as a candidate distinction not currently in the law; together with standing (S1-F032's 'was this input allowed to participate?'), identifies a converging triple of independent admission conditions: standing, prerequisite presence, context sufficiency.
missing: formalization of context sufficiency

rows.anchor: Knowledge changes when evidence changes. ... re-assessment of an acquisition procedure could change knowledge state retroactively. No document draws that; recorded as an open consequence.
rows.statement: Records 'knowledge changes when evidence changes' as a dependency claim with an undrawn temporal consequence: combined with S1-F030's claim that acquisition constitutes evidential status, re-assessment of an acquisition procedure could change knowledge state retroactively — a consequence no source document states, recorded here as an open implication; also records 'uncertainty is not the same thing as truth' as a recurrence of the existing probability≠truth rule from statistics.
missing: whether retroactive knowledge-state change is acceptable or must be blocked

rows.anchor: Candidate / hypothesis requiring later architectural investigation.
rows.statement: Records a session-handover document's practice of labeling each extracted item with an explicit status ('candidate / hypothesis requiring later architectural investigation') rather than leaving classification to a later reader, identified as a sixth instance of the research-must-not-become-architecture discipline, and the only one implemented as a per-item label.

rows.anchor: Good: It correctly captured your latest conceptual breakthrough. ... Needs caution: Some "mathematical evidence" is actually hypothesis. We should not assume Facts are probabilistic objects. We should not assume a measurable-space ontology. We should not assume the exact Closure() formulation yet.
rows.statement: Gives a final good/needs-caution assessment of the Perplexity document: correctly captures the probability-vs-logic division and the Fact Problem and correctly recommends not designing the Kernel yet; but needs caution because several items labeled mathematical evidence are actually hypotheses (Facts as probabilistic objects, a measurable-space ontology, the exact Closure() formulation), and independent research is needed before turning any of this into definitions; concludes the next research focus should be exclusively 'Fact', the missing bridge between what is observed and what is known.

rows.anchor: a sufficiently safe decision ... adequacy is relative to use.
rows.statement: Notes sufficient state is decision-relative like S1-F029's abstention threshold, giving two independent sources making an epistemic adequacy criterion depend on the decision it must support rather than on the claim alone, flagged as a recurring shape: adequacy is relative to use.

rows.anchor: Do not confuse the observable representation with the underlying state. ... Language is a projection of meaning, not the container of meaning.
rows.statement: Records Fraser's distinction (observable ≠ underlying state) as the fourth independent route to the corpus's Expression≠Meaning/Representation≠Identity rule, reached from state-space modelling; records 'language is a projection of meaning, not the container of meaning' as a sixth distinct sense of the word 'projection' in the corpus (naming the representation->meaning relation, not a view/measure/read-model/derived-attribute), registered as a vocabulary-collision addition, not merged with earlier senses.

rows.anchor: What must exist before inference is legitimate? ... What problem does each technique solve? What concept does it embody? What responsibility does it have? What invariant does it preserve? ... Numerical stability is part of assurance.
rows.statement: Records a legitimacy precondition for inference ('what must exist before inference is legitimate?') as a third arrival at the inference-licensing family, here framed as a precondition rather than a prohibition; records a four-part method frame (problem/concept/responsibility/invariant) as the only place in the corpus requiring every imported technique to declare which invariant it preserves; records 'numerical stability is part of assurance' as quietly enlarging assurance from an epistemic to an implementation property — the only such claim found, classified as implementation evidence.

rows.anchor: Assessment is not the same thing as Observation, Evidence, Recommendation, or Decision.
rows.statement: Records a five-way non-collapse (Assessment ≠ Observation, Evidence, Recommendation, Decision), completing a Phase-1 sequence claim (Observation->Recommendation->Decision->Outcome->Assessment) by asserting the members are mutually irreducible, not merely sequential; bears on S1-F014 by supporting (not resolving) the classification of INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE as an assessment versus CONTESTED as a relationship, which S1-F018 disputed.

rows.anchor: remove as much prior structure as possible and ask what can be recovered from the source/data alone ... the Zero lens is defined on 2026-08-24 at 15:24 while it has been in continuous use since 2026-08-23 ... a ~17-hour definition lag.
rows.statement: Records the Zero-lens's own definition ('remove as much prior structure as possible and ask what can be recovered from the source/data alone; if we assume nothing about what the structure is supposed to be, what structure can we actually observe?'), flagging a provenance caveat: the lens was in continuous use from 2026-08-23 but only formally defined here at 2026-08-24 15:24, a roughly 17-hour lag, meaning earlier Zero-lens-derived findings (including S1-F013, S1-F016, S1-F021) used an undefined instrument — recorded as a caveat, not an invalidation.

rows.anchor: How can meaning be represented, transformed, combined, and expressed without losing semantic identity? ... When something changes its form, how do we know that its identity and meaning have been preserved? ... Does the text actually contain ten statistically distinct problem-solving mechanisms?
rows.statement: Records Sanskrit/Paninian material's identity-preservation question as a fifth arrival at identity-through-change (after S1-F015, F022, F026, F031), framed here as transformation-invariance, matching the Escher lens's assigned role from S1-F021; records a disciplined refusal to accept a source's own taxonomy count without checking distinctness ('does the text actually contain ten statistically distinct problem-solving mechanisms?') as the same ativyapti (over-inclusion) discipline as S1-F023.

rows.anchor: How did this evidence produce the conclusion, and how robust is that relationship? ... Would the system still have arrived at the correct conclusion under relevant counterfactual variations?
rows.statement: Introduces counterfactual robustness as the corpus's first checkable test (rather than prohibition or precondition) for an evidence-to-conclusion link: would the system still reach the correct conclusion under relevant counterfactual variation; notes, as an unremarked convergence, that counterfactual variation is precisely how one would obtain validation evidence distinct from construction evidence, the mechanism S1-F029's construction/validation separation lacked.
missing: operationalization of 'relevant counterfactual variations'

rows.anchor: A knowledge claim should carry not only its content, but the epistemic route by which it was obtained. ... Analogy is not observation.
rows.statement: Records the sharpest of three arrivals at route/source retention (after Audi's source-type retention and S1-F030's constitutive acquisition): a knowledge claim should carry the epistemic route by which it was obtained, illustrated by the pramana distinction upamana (analogy) ≠ pratyaksa (observation); combined with S1-F029 (role) and S1-F030 (acquisition), identifies (as its own inference) three separate things an evidence/claim reference may need to carry: route, acquisition procedure, and role; notes 'route' is adjacent to but not identical with a separate ledger's justification-path obligation (route = by what epistemic means obtained; justification path = how the conclusion follows).

rows.anchor: The knowledge state became more complete, but less certain. ... if adding knowledge lowers certainty, then Confidence cannot be monotone in evidence volume
rows.statement: Records the only place across 93 processed documents where completeness and certainty are said to trade against each other ('the knowledge state became more complete, but less certain'), rather than being independently desirable; draws the direct consequence for Confidence derivation: if adding knowledge can lower certainty, Confidence cannot be monotone in evidence volume, foreclosing the simplest derivations of it.

rows.anchor: Knowledge is not located at one level of representation. It emerges from relationships between levels. ... At which level does a particular knowledge structure become meaningful?
rows.statement: Records Hofstadter's (GEB) claim that knowledge emerges from relationships between levels rather than being located at one level, registered as a seventh genus for Knowledge in the corpus's series (distinct from relationship, state, product, capacity, ratified commitment, understanding); its architectural bite is that any single-altitude Kernel (kernel/mechanism/representation, or any of the corpus's boundary formulations) cannot contain a phenomenon that is inherently inter-level — a challenge of a different shape from all eight prior Kernel formulations; flagged as single-sourced.

rows.anchor: Which invariants must remain valid regardless of epistemic state? ... Zero is not 'nothing.' ... the minimum invariant structure that survives changes in representation.
rows.statement: Records a catuskoti-derived question ('which invariants must remain valid regardless of epistemic state?') as cutting against the four-valued epistemic-status proposal made in the same source documents — separating invariant layer from state layer argues for fewer states, not more; records 'Zero is not nothing' and 'the minimum invariant structure that survives changes in representation' as the closest the corpus comes to defining what the Zero lens is for, aligning with the 'boring Kernel' principle; classified as partial internal resistance to the documents' own state-adding proposal.

rows.anchor: We should not assume these form a simple sequence. ... Perhaps the structure is a partial order, not a linear state machine. Or perhaps "superseded" isn't a state at all. It may be: K_1 ≺ K_2 where K_2 supersedes K_1.
rows.statement: Applies order theory to the epistemic-state set (Unknown, Validated, Rejected, Conflicted, Superseded), warning against assuming a simple linear sequence (Unknown<Validated but Validated not< Rejected suggests a partial order), and proposing 'superseded' may not be a state at all but a relation K1≺K2 (K2 supersedes K1) — connecting to the corpus's unresolved question of whether SUPERSEDED/RECONCILED/CONTESTED/INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE are states, relationships, events, assessments, or derived conditions.

rows.anchor: we must not automatically equate: Confidence(F)=P(F). That would be an architectural assumption, not a discovery.
rows.statement: Applies the probability lens to Confidence(F), asking whether it is P(F|E), an ordinal assessment (Low<Medium<High), or a domain-specific value, warning that automatically equating Confidence(F)=P(F) would be an unearned architectural assumption rather than a research discovery.

rows.anchor: Where did the first determinations come from? ... Observation → Evidence → Determination → Fact → Future Evidence → New Determination ... Knowledge has memory, but memory itself is not knowledge. ... Gaṇeśa lens — observation → memory → discrimination → revision → integration
rows.statement: Poses the regress question of where the first determinations came from, tracing the chain back to Observation -> Evidence -> Determination -> Fact -> Future Evidence -> New Determination, concluding 'Knowledge has memory, but memory itself is not knowledge,' and connecting this to the Ganesha lens (observation->memory->discrimination->revision->integration); proposes the deeper research question 'how does a system move from what happened, to what was determined about what happened, to what can subsequently be used as a basis for determining something else?' as potentially more fundamental than the Candidate->Knowledge model.
missing: answer to the regress question
invariants: Knowledge has memory, but memory itself is not knowledge.

rows.anchor: Do not automatically turn every fundamental concept into an aggregate of lower-level database constructs. ... Do not derive the ontology from the representation format. ... Do not solve a primitive concept by renaming it.
rows.statement: The corpus's own day-four self-diagnosis yields three modelling prohibitions: (1) do not automatically turn every fundamental concept into an aggregate of lower-level database constructs -- mapped as the cause of the prior god-aggregate finding (S1-F007) and its four member-list decompositions of Identity/Evidence/Confidence/History; (2) do not derive the ontology from the representation format -- the general form of S1-F027's inference-licensing rule (never infer ontology from representation), restated as a modelling rather than inference rule, and the general form of Ledger v1.1's C-1 (canonical-form equality is not identity); (3) do not solve a primitive concept by renaming it -- naming the recurring temptation the census registered: KnowledgeClaim -> KnowledgeElement -> 'identity-bearing, contextualized assertion record' -> Assertion, four names for what may be one unresolved primitive (ledger PS-1).
invariants: never decompose a fundamental concept into an aggregate merely to make it storable
never derive ontology from representation format
never treat renaming a primitive as having solved it

lineage_claims.quote: The first is what produced the god-aggregate (S1-F007) and the four member lists
The second is S1-F027's inference-licensing family ... restated as a modelling rule rather than an inference rule

rows.anchor: Identity is unitary, primitive, and indefinable, and Existence is a first-order property, contra Russell's quantifier view. ... CONSISTENT with INV-KOS-IDENTITY-001's assigned, never derived -- but ... arrives at the same place from the opposite direction to S1-F031's ziran challenge ... and to S1-F016 (identity merely administrative). Three positions on identity now stand unreconciled: primitive-and-indefinable, self-so-not-assigned, administrative.
rows.statement: McGinn's claim that identity is unitary, primitive, and indefinable (with existence a first-order property, against Russell's quantifier view) is consistent with INV-KOS-IDENTITY-001's 'assigned, never derived' stance, but arrives there from the opposite direction of S1-F031's ziran/self-so challenge (identity too fundamental to be assigned) and S1-F016's administrative-identity view; three positions on identity (primitive-and-indefinable, self-so-not-assigned, administrative) now stand unreconciled in the corpus.
missing: reconciliation of the three identity positions

lineage_claims.target: S1-F031 (ziran/self-so identity challenge) and S1-F016 (administrative identity)
lineage_claims.quote: Three positions on identity now stand unreconciled

rows.anchor: A Knowledge Space boundary should normally be a boundary of abstraction, purpose, scope and observability. ... its four terms are all observer-relative ... That makes Knowledge-Space boundaries categorically different from the Kernel boundary, which every formulation treats as invariant-determined and observer-independent. Two boundary concepts, one word. Registered as a VOCABULARY COLLISION (boundary) -- the corpus's seventh collision.
rows.statement: Defines a Knowledge-Space boundary as a boundary of abstraction, purpose, scope, and observability -- all four terms observer-relative -- categorically different from the Kernel boundary, which every formulation treats as invariant-determined and observer-independent; registers 'boundary' as the corpus's seventh vocabulary collision (after Kernel [4 senses], projection [6], agent, UNKNOWN, C-1, altitude/boundary).
invariants: a Knowledge-Space boundary (observer-relative) must never be conflated with the Kernel boundary (invariant-determined)

rows.anchor: Persons are not merely objects inside Knowledge Space. They are participants that traverse and transform Knowledge Space. ... Is this a primitive entity, a relation, a property, a state, a representation, a perspective, or merely a useful projection? ... extended from three options to seven, and applicable to any candidate.
rows.statement: Distinguishes participants (persons) as entities that traverse and transform Knowledge Space, not merely objects inside it; if participants transform the space, per-participant divergence is a change to the space, a stronger claim than 'different projections of one fixed space'. Introduces a seven-way classification test applicable to any candidate concept -- is it a primitive entity, a relation, a property, a state, a representation, a perspective, or merely a useful projection -- extending S1-F013's three-way state/relationship/event blocker to seven options.

lineage_claims.quote: extended from three options to seven, and applicable to any candidate

rows.anchor: Is Knowledge Space fundamentally a space of information, or is information itself only one layer inside Knowledge Space? ... What is knowledge itself? ... information is not the same thing as meaning ... KnowledgeOS should be representation-independent. ... after ~150 documents, the corpus asks what is knowledge itself ... consistent with the Knowledge-genus series remaining at seven unreconciled genera.
rows.statement: Records that after roughly 150 documents, the corpus itself still asks whether Knowledge Space is fundamentally a space of information or whether information is only one layer inside it, and what knowledge itself is; Dretske's contribution is that information is not the same thing as meaning and that KnowledgeOS should be representation-independent; recorded as a coverage fact confirming S1-F026 (the book programme produced distinctions, not a definition), consistent with the Knowledge-genus series remaining at seven unreconciled genera.

lineage_claims.target: S1-F026 (book programme produced distinctions, not a definition)
lineage_claims.quote: it confirms what S1-F026 declared

rows.anchor: Store the substrate; compute the measure. ... coverage of a declared finite inquiry boundary. ... the substrate is preserved and every measure is derived, which satisfies S1-F032's "there is no single Knowledge Score" without abandoning measurement.
rows.statement: Design principle 'store the substrate; compute the measure': the substrate is preserved and every measure (entropy, Confidence, a Knowledge Score, a measure-theoretic projection) is derived from it rather than stored as a member itself; satisfies the prior 'no single Knowledge Score' finding (S1-F032) without abandoning measurement, is consistent with Ledger v1.1's r4 (interpretation probabilities are port-contract vocabulary, never aggregate members), and bears (as research evidence only, not a ruling) on open questions about whether Confidence should be derivable/an aggregate member. Coverage is always relative to a declared finite inquiry boundary, not global.
invariants: measures are always derived from the stored substrate, never stored themselves as substrate members
measurement coverage is scoped to a declared finite inquiry boundary, never global

lineage_claims.quote: satisfies S1-F032's "there is no single Knowledge Score" without abandoning measurement

rows.anchor: "What did we know at 13:47?" ... The single most concrete acceptance test in the corpus. It is checkable, it is temporal, and it is the question S1-F001 measured the system as unable to answer (0/20 grants carry validity information). ... it also operationalises S1-F034's sufficient state.
rows.statement: Names 'What did we know at 13:47?' as the single most concrete acceptance test in the corpus -- checkable and temporal -- and the same question S1-F001 measured the system as currently unable to answer (0/20 grants carry validity information); it operationalizes S1-F034's 'sufficient state' as whatever must be retained for this question to be answerable at an arbitrary past instant. Together with S1-F036's 'why/when did X change', the corpus now has two point-in-time acceptance tests plus one representability test (S1-F027); none has been run.
missing: actually running any of the three acceptance/representability tests

lineage_claims.target: S1-F001 (0/20 grants carry validity information) and S1-F034 (sufficient state)
lineage_claims.quote: it is the question S1-F001 measured the system as unable to answer

rows.anchor: Different projections must never contain contradictory propositions. A projection becomes more informative or structurally adequate relative to a defined inquiry and boundary. ... divergence is permitted in coverage, forbidden in content. ... it sits in tension with S1-F037's participants who transform the space.
rows.statement: Candidate projection-consistency invariant: different projections must never contain contradictory propositions, though a projection may become more informative or structurally adequate relative to a defined inquiry/boundary -- divergence is permitted in coverage but forbidden in content. Answers whether two projections can differ without knowledge differing (yes in informativeness, no in consistency). Single-sourced, and in explicit tension with S1-F037's claim that participants transform the space (if participants transform the space, contradictory projections could be legitimate) -- recorded, unresolved.
missing: reconciliation with S1-F037's transforming-participants claim
invariants: projections may diverge in coverage/informativeness but must never contain mutually contradictory propositions

lineage_claims.quote: it sits in tension with S1-F037's participants who transform the space

rows.anchor: What is the minimal representation of an epistemic state, and how does that state change? ... KnowledgeOS should not store an epistemic state as "possible worlds." ... converges with the Fagin thread's own resolution (possible-worlds semantics as a supported regime, not the Kernel).
rows.statement: Gaerdenfors reframes the question from 'what is knowledge' to 'what is the minimal representation of an epistemic state, and how does that state change', and explicitly refuses one specific formal storage model by name: KnowledgeOS should not store an epistemic state as 'possible worlds' -- converging independently with the Fagin thread's resolution that possible-worlds semantics is a supported regime, not the Kernel itself; this is the same contain/derive split as the substrate/measure principle, applied at the state level rather than the measure level.
invariants: an epistemic state is never stored as a possible-worlds structure in the Kernel

rows.anchor: Knowledge is always knowledge-at-a-time within an evolving Knowledge Space. ... Absence must not silently become an epistemic state. ... The Knowledge Space is not necessarily the same thing as any one model of it ... KnowledgeOS should preserve and serve that space, rather than pretending to own the whole of knowledge. ... this document is the one whose attribution of the Knowledge-Space model to "your earlier conceptual model" was tested and not supported by the Phase 1 corpus.
rows.statement: Two further temporal/scope claims: (1) knowledge is always knowledge-at-a-time within an evolving Knowledge Space, and absence must not silently become an epistemic state -- the ninth independent angle on the absence/retraction family, consistent with Ledger's Z-1 (absence of a constitutive prerequisite is not an epistemic state); (2) the Knowledge Space is not necessarily the same thing as any one model of it, and KnowledgeOS should preserve and serve that space rather than pretending to own the whole of knowledge (a scope-humility claim compatible with the KnowledgeOS superset KnowledgeCore superset Kernel nesting, adding an outer layer the ADR does not name). Explicit provenance caution: this source document's attribution of the Knowledge-Space model to an earlier conceptual model was tested and NOT supported by the Phase 1 corpus; its claims stand only as Phase 2 positions.
invariants: absence must never silently become an epistemic state

lineage_claims.quote: the closest to L Z-1 ... CONSISTENT, reached independently

rows.anchor: The Kernel preserves the structures that enable discrimination; reasoning regimes perform the discrimination. ... KnowledgeOS Kernel should not itself be 'the reasoning engine.' ... Reasoning bridges the gap between what is represented and what is believed ... four independent sources ... arrive at the same split: structures preserved / reasoning performed elsewhere.
rows.statement: The corpus's most convergent architectural claim, reached independently by four sources (a project synthesis, Gelfond & Kahl's KR&R, Brachman & Levesque's KR&R, and Brandom's inferentialism): the Kernel preserves the structures that enable discrimination; reasoning regimes perform the discrimination -- the Kernel should not itself be 'the reasoning engine'.
