rows.statement: Step 213 ('Evidence-First Reconstruction') defines the F/D/P/U epistemic label (Fact/Derived/Proposed/Unknown); the Experience->Problem->Observation->Experiment->Pattern->Abstraction->Theory->Architecture chain; evidence extraction E(A_j)={Facts,Observations,Decisions,Assumptions,Experiments,Failures,Questions}; Artifact->Evidence->Interpretation; provenance of architecture Prov(C)={A_1,...,A_n}; Architecture Decision Lineage ADL=Decision->Problem->Evidence->Alternatives->Rationale->Consequence; 'What did not work' / 'what eventually worked' (the negative-result principle); an architecture-as-state-machine A_{t+1}=E(A_t,Evidence_t); the change record DeltaA=(Trigger,Evidence,Decision,Rationale,Impact); O->D->P with P⇏O; boxes 'AI Interpretation != Engineering Evidence'; boxes EAG=(Evidence,Claims,Decisions,Invariants,Architecture) and the closed loop Observation->Knowledge->Architecture->Invariant->Implementation->Test->Evidence->NewKnowledge; and boxes 'every significant architectural claim should have an evidence lineage' / 'every significant architectural change should have a reason lineage'.

rows.anchor: PREVIOUS DEPENDENCY: ZERO individual prior steps (one range, Steps 1-182); LATER RESPONSE: Steps 214 and 215 both build on F/D/P/U
rows.statement: Step 213 cites zero individual prior steps by number, only the Steps-1-182 range (in the Step-214 preview). Later response in scope: Step 214 Section 214.1 operationalizes F/D/P/U into the 10-tuple EL_i; Step 215 Section 215.4 adopts F/D/P/U as its second classification axis.

rows.anchor: EVOLUTION VERDICT: REFRAMES, with the 212->213 mapping never stated (five-valued implementation status vs four-valued epistemic status)
rows.statement: Step 213 converts Step 212's five-valued implementation Status into a four-valued epistemic F/D/P/U status, but the relation between them is never stated -- is Specified (212) the same as P (213)? Is Unknown (212) the same as U (213)? The file does not say, leaving two five/four-valued scales over overlapping ground unmapped. DEFINITION VERDICT: CLEAR -- F/D/P/U is well defined, well motivated, well illustrated (Section 213.23's three-level worked example is the clearest pedagogy in the band), and the primary/secondary evidence split (Section 213.28: primary = source code/config/schema/test result/runtime behavior/direct experiment; secondary = AI analysis/architecture summary/meeting notes/retrospective explanation) is precise.

rows.anchor: DERIVATION VERDICT: VALID_WITH_ASSUMPTIONS — the strongest derivation verdict in the band; no first invalid inference identified
rows.statement: O->D->P but P⇏O (Section 213.24, 'a proposal cannot retroactively become evidence for the observation that motivated it') is correct reasoning with no invalid inference found. Section 213.25 correctly identifies its own potential circularity ('we need deterministic assurance because KnowledgeOS is a deterministic assurance platform -- that is circular') and Section 213.32 blocks the meta-circularity ('we must not say the method is correct because it follows the architecture'). The one type-level irritant noted (not an invalid inference): E is bound to evidence extraction in Section 213.4 and to the architecture-evolution operator in Section 213.17, thirteen sections apart, in a file about not conflating things -- 'operator drift'.

rows.anchor: COMPUTABILITY: F/D/P/U applied 0 times; Prov(C), EAG, ADL, DeltaA all DEFINED with 0 instances; TEST VERDICT NOT_EXECUTED
rows.statement: F/D/P/U is DEFINED but applied 0 times (the four bracket-form occurrences at lines 754-757 are the legend itself); E(A_j) extraction is DEFINED with 0 artifacts extracted; Prov(C), EAG, ADL are each DEFINED with 0 instances; DeltaA 5-tuple is DEFINED with 0 changes recorded. TEST VERDICT NOT_EXECUTED -- the single regex hit is a verified false positive; no test, artifact, or read.

rows.anchor: STATISTICAL VERDICT: VERY STRONG (the negative-result principle is the best methodological passage in the band); MEASUREMENT VERDICT: CORRECT — the only file in the band with no scale violation
rows.statement: Sections 213.13-213.14's negative-result principle ('a failed experiment is not useless... some of the strongest architectural principles may originate from failed approaches... otherwise the final architecture looks inevitable, real engineering is not inevitable') is publication-bias awareness, correct and important, judged the best methodological passage in the eight files. Section 213.27's insistence that confidence be assigned only when justified is correct. Measurement: F/D/P/U is nominal and treated as nominal, Confidence is ordinal (High/Medium) with no arithmetic, Prov(C) is a set with membership-only operations -- no arithmetic is performed on any scale in Step 213, the only file in the band with no scale violation.

rows.anchor: DDD VERDICT: STRONG (the six change-governance questions map cleanly onto DDD); UL: F/D/P/U enters cleanly but E is overloaded to breaking point and Evidence now has six bindings
rows.statement: Section 213.36's six change-governance questions (what changed, why, which invariant is affected, which bounded context owns it, what evidence justifies it, how was it verified) map cleanly onto DDD, and Section 213.12's ADL is essentially an ADR strengthened with an evidence and alternatives column. Deficiency: no bounded context is named anywhere in the file. UL: F/D/P/U enters the language cleanly, but E is now overloaded (see Part 5 symbol drift), and 'Evidence' itself is now: a bounded context (208), a node class V_F (211), a graph vertex set (213.33), a strength level E_n (210, 212), a tuple slot (210.1, 212.3, 214.1), and a column header (215) -- six bindings of the corpus's most load-bearing noun.

rows.anchor: ASSUMPTIONS / HIDDEN ASSUMPTIONS — the classifier applying F/D/P/U is itself the AI it warns against; WHAT SURVIVES: the most of any file in the band
rows.statement: Assumptions: artifacts persist and are retrievable; every statement admits exactly one of F/D/P/U; primary evidence is available. Hidden: that the classification will actually be applied (it is not, in this file or the next two); that F/D/P/U is exhaustive (no slot for a contradicted claim, though Step 214 later makes contradiction a first-class edge); that the classifier is disinterested -- Section 213.29 correctly flags AI as secondary evidence, but the classifier here is the AI itself, noticed in Section 213.31 ('we are using AI to reconstruct an architecture for an AI engineering platform') without resolution -- Section 213.32's proposed resolution (Evidence+Reproducibility+Traceability) is satisfied by none of the three in this band. Undefined symbols: the satisfaction relation in Evidence(A) |= F, g/h in D=g(O)/P=h(D), the evolution operator E(.,.), e_1..e_n, Confidence(C) codomain. Survives (the most of any file in the band): F/D/P/U as a discipline; AI Interpretation != Engineering Evidence; O->D->P with P⇏O; the negative-result principle; primary vs secondary evidence; Prov(C); the archaeological question 'what does this artifact actually establish?'; Section 213.8's model sentence, 'provenance enforcement could not yet be established from the available evidence' (the correct form of an honest negative finding). Nothing is refuted; everything is unexecuted.

rows.anchor: A and Gap: eight bindings of A, four bindings of Gap with two different ordinal category sets
rows.statement: A denotes: Assessment (208-212, throughout), an aggregate state A_t (209.13), the architecture-as-CSP set A (209.34), an assurance vector (211.9), an AI-artifact 7-tuple (211.21), a statistical-result 8-tuple (210.13), an architecture snapshot A_t (213.16-18), and an artifact A_j (213.4) -- eight bindings, with Section 209.13's aggregate-state A_t formally indistinguishable in notation from Section 213.17-18's architecture-state A_t (delta(A_t,c)=A_{t+1} vs A_0->A_1->...). Gap denotes: a numeric difference (211.4, 212.10), an ordinal category (211.4's {None,Low,Medium,High,Critical} vs 212.10's different {None,Partial,Significant,Critical,Unknown}), a class (212.11 G1-G5), and a register row (212.31 G-01-G-15) -- four bindings, with the two ordinal category sets differing from each other.

rows.statement: Step 213 Section 213.26 mandates that every important statement during reconstruction carry an [F]/[D]/[P]/[U] label ('our editorial control system'). sources.note: KOS-ARCH-BASELINE-001, the Phase-A current-state architecture reconstruction and its correction/verification chain.

rows.anchor: D-1 · Hook count wrong: Phase A says 8, actual is 10 ... the total was eyeballed rather than computed
rows.statement: D-1: Phase A's high-confidence Observed claim of 8 wired hooks is wrong; the actual count via a JSON-parsing method is 10 (PreToolUse 5, PostToolUse 2, SessionStart 1, Stop 2), the original figure having been eyeballed rather than computed, with settings.json unchanged since the baseline commit ruling out temporal drift.

rows.anchor: D-2 · 'Four of seven components have no executable substance' — false, and self-contradicting ... Phase A's own §3.1 table already says this
rows.statement: D-2: the claim that four of seven components have no executable substance is false (the actual figure is two of eight zero-asset components) and self-contradicting, since Phase A's own detail table already correctly marks two other components PARTIAL rather than NONE.

rows.anchor: D-3 · An unflagged declared-vs-registry discrepancy ... the composition root, the component that wires everything
rows.statement: D-3: Phase A uses '7' and '8' components in different sentences without noting they disagree; the frozen reference architecture declares seven components and omits the composition root, while the live registry carries eight including CMP-001 composition_root with two assets, a miss of exactly the declared-vs-executing gap the document exists to catch.

rows.anchor: VERDICT — THE BASELINE IS A FAITHFUL RECONSTRUCTION WITH FOUR PRECISION DEFECTS, NONE STRUCTURAL ... 11 of 12 sampled Observed claims re-derived TRUE
rows.statement: Independent verification confirms Phase A is a faithful reconstruction with four precision defects, none structural: 11 of 12 sampled Observed claims and all four Declared mechanism probes re-derived true, and all three producer-disclosed defects (D-1/D-2/D-3) confirmed.

rows.anchor: V-A · Phase A §6's own diagram sums to 10 while its caption says 8 ... it upgrades D-1 from miscount to internal inconsistency
rows.statement: V-A (new finding): the same document's own §6 diagram already sums to 10 hooks while its caption says 8, a same-page self-contradiction of D-2's exact shape, showing the correct number was already present inside the document.

rows.anchor: V-E · '8 workflow records' is retroactively unverifiable — because of Phase A's own finding. ... the baseline's own snapshot number inherits the no-provenance defect it reports.
rows.statement: V-E: the workflow-record count in the baseline is retroactively unverifiable because the records are gitignored with no history, meaning the baseline's own snapshot figure inherits the very no-provenance defect its thesis reports; recorded as an acceptance-context fact, not an error.

rows.anchor: VERDICT — VERIFIED WITH NOTES ... Canonical acceptance should wait until N-1 and N-2 are corrected.
rows.statement: Verification #2 confirms all seven of v1.1's producer repairs (D-1, D-2, D-3, V-A, V-B, V-C, V-D) as correctly applied from primary evidence, but recommends acceptance wait until two new document-integrity defects introduced by the correction itself are fixed.

rows.anchor: N-1 (MODERATE) — same class as the defects repaired ... Line 1 is still v1.0 ... line 6 declares v1.1
rows.statement: N-1 (new defect): the corrected document's own title line still says v1.0 while its version banner says v1.1, exactly the same self-contradiction shape the correction round was convened to repair, though it changes no conclusion.

rows.anchor: N-2 | MINOR — presentational | §6.4 is placed before §6.3.
rows.statement: N-2 (new defect): the newly inserted §6.4 section is placed before §6.3 in reading order, an out-of-order numbering artifact of the insertion mechanics, not the analysis.

rows.anchor: Classification of what remains: document-integrity defects, NOT domain-model defects.
rows.statement: N-1 and N-2 are explicitly classified as document-integrity defects, not domain-model defects: they change no bounded context, aggregate, invariant, ownership, dependency direction, authority boundary, or current-state conclusion, warranting a proportionate document-consistency pass rather than another reconstruction round.

rows.anchor: Title line only; no content, finding, snapshot or classification touched. ... The identifier 6.4 is preserved — the block was moved, never renumbered
rows.statement: The N-1/N-2 correction is delivered as two minimal, mechanically scoped edits: the title character changed to agree with the version banner, and the §6.4 block moved (never renumbered) below §6.3 so all existing references to §6.4 remain valid.

rows.anchor: The PO/ARB's prompt listed as source 1: 'Original Verification #2' ... That file is Verification #1 ... Corrected in the grant ... with the correction disclosed rather than silently applied.
rows.statement: Governance detects and corrects, rather than silently propagating, a wrong file reference in the delivered commissioning prompt (it named Verification #1's file as if it were Verification #2), noting it is the third instance of this same referent-checking-class error in the programme.

rows.anchor: There is no lane, no START and no grant under which Verification #2 was performed. ... its independence is not recorded anywhere.
rows.statement: Verification #2 (the phase-a-v1.1-correction-verification report) is found to have run under no recorded lane, grant, or START at all; its content is not disputed, but its independence cannot be attested from the record, which INV-ATTR-2 already predicts as a limitation.

rows.anchor: This work item's evidence chain now spans two documentation roots ... php scripts/doc-placement.php returns no matching rule.
rows.statement: For a work item whose subject is evidence integrity, its own evidence chain is observed to be split unresolved across two documentation roots (docs/publicdigit/reviews and docs/knowledgeos/reviews), with the placement resolver returning no matching rule for this case; recorded as an observation only, with no files moved.

rows.anchor: VERDICT — N-1: PASS · N-2: PASS · all integrity checks: PASS ... exactly two hunks: the title character and a byte-identical block move.
rows.statement: Verification #3 confirms the N-1/N-2 correction did exactly what was authorized and nothing else, closing the entire Phase-A correction chain (Verification #1 -> v1.1 -> Verification #2 -> N-1/N-2 correction -> this report) with no outstanding verified defect.

rows.anchor: All references still resolve ... Had the block been renumbered instead of moved, all seven references would now dangle
rows.statement: Independent re-derivation confirms all seven references to §6.4 across the baseline and Verification #2 still resolve correctly because the block was moved rather than renumbered, demonstrating the referential-integrity discipline did real protective work.

rows.anchor: Record acceptance only of the verification evidence. Do not accept the architecture baseline in this act. ... Then wait for the separate baseline acceptance act.
rows.statement: The PO/ARB explicitly accepts only the Verification #3 evidence, deliberately deferring acceptance of the Phase-A baseline artifact itself to a separate, later act -- a disciplined separation of evidence-acceptance from artifact-acceptance.

rows.anchor: The PO/ARB accepts the Current Architecture Baseline Phase A v1.1 as the authoritative reconstructed current-state architecture baseline.
rows.statement: Phase A v1.1 is formally accepted into the canon as the authoritative current-state architecture baseline and the foundation for Stage 2 analysis only, not approving bounded contexts, aggregates, implementation architecture, technology, or migration.

rows.anchor: Taken with eyes open — V-E ... the snapshot numbers can never be retroactively audited. The PO/ARB accepts the baseline knowing this.
rows.statement: The acceptance act explicitly incorporates the V-E limitation: the baseline's machine-state figures are declarations of a moment that left no trace (gitignored, no history) and can never be retroactively audited, and the PO/ARB accepts the baseline knowing this rather than treating it as resolved.

rows.anchor: G0 PKS 'documentation/instruction system' → self-correction → G1 PKS knowledge system YAML+Markdown+Git → G2 KnowledgeOS proposal 6 bounded contexts → G3 EKS proposal 7 contexts→4 contexts+planes PostgreSQL-centric → G3/v3 reconciliation returns to: repository system of record.
rows.statement: Traces four successive historical architecture 'generations' of PKS/EKS/KnowledgeOS naming and positioning, showing a reversal from a certified repository-as-system-of-record position through a PostgreSQL-centric proposal and back to a repository-centric reconciliation.

rows.anchor: Prior state: ... ⛔ BROKEN/INCOMPLETE marker at file top; file ends at §20 (line 1162); its own body cross-references terminal sections that do not exist: §21 ... §22 ... §23 ... §24 ... §25 ... Not a valid P1 deliverable as delivered.
rows.statement: Before this commission, the EKS Current Architecture Baseline document was marked BROKEN/INCOMPLETE: it ended at §20 while its own body cross-referenced terminal sections §21 (special questions), §22, §23 (P-rows), §24 (UNKNOWN register U-*), and §25 (contradiction register X-*) that did not yet exist -- explicitly recorded as 'not a valid P1 deliverable as delivered.'

rows.anchor: DO NOT rewrite the existing EKS baseline §1–§20. DO NOT construct the EKS–PKS–AIP landscape (that is P4). DO NOT classify shared concepts. DO NOT create the reconciliation ledger. DO NOT identify kernel candidates. DO NOT run the AMENDMENT-6 progression (that is P5). DO NOT design KnowledgeOS. DO NOT propose evolution. DO NOT use the proposed KnowledgeOS architecture ... to interpret EKS current architecture. DO NOT unify similar-looking concepts ... DO NOT mistake an implementation mechanism for the invariant it protects
rows.statement: The commission's DO-NOT list bounds a fresh isolated read-only session strictly to corpus completion: no rewriting §1-20, no landscape construction, no shared-concept classification, no reconciliation ledger, no kernel-candidate identification, no AMENDMENT-6 progression, no KnowledgeOS design or evolution proposal, no use of the proposed (quarantined) KnowledgeOS architecture Review Set to interpret EKS, no unifying similar-looking concepts, and no conflating an implementation mechanism with the invariant it protects.

rows.anchor: Corpus-boundary rule (P2/P3 precedent): §5.3 is the governed starting corpus, not necessarily exhaustive. Any additional EKS evidence admitted is admitted by role, with a recorded finding — corpus-boundary decisions are findings, never silent choices.
rows.statement: Corpus-boundary rule carried from P2/P3 precedent: the governed starting corpus is not assumed exhaustive; any additional evidence admitted into the reconstruction must be admitted by explicit role with a recorded finding -- corpus-boundary decisions are findings, never silent choices.

rows.anchor: P3-F1 lesson (binding): the MIGRATION-PLAN incident — a 196KB artifact whose unread internal body contained current-state facts (23/30 concurrent-append trials; KOS_MECHANISM_PATH write surface) that overturned the baseline's completeness claim. Distinguish NOT FOUND ≠ NOT PRESENT ≠ NOT EVIDENCED ≠ UNKNOWN. Before concluding 'not found', the corpus must be exhaustively checked. An honest UNKNOWN is valid; an artificial UNKNOWN is a defect.
rows.statement: The 'P3-F1 lesson' is recorded as binding precedent: an unread 196KB artifact's internal body held current-state facts (a 23/30 concurrent-append-loss trial rate; a write-capable KOS_MECHANISM_PATH surface) that overturned an earlier baseline's completeness claim once actually read. The lesson distinguishes NOT FOUND ≠ NOT PRESENT ≠ NOT EVIDENCED ≠ UNKNOWN, requires exhaustive corpus reading before concluding 'not found', and holds that an honest UNKNOWN is valid while an artificial (unearned) UNKNOWN is itself a defect.

rows.anchor: Evidence-first. Every substantive claim carries (a) an evidence tier (1–8, strongest = implementation), (b) a reality class A–G ... or (c) a stable UNKNOWN/register reference. No B/C/G finding is promoted to A. Documentation describing a desired behaviour is never evidence that it is implemented.
rows.statement: Method carried forward from P2/P3: every substantive claim must carry an evidence tier (1-8, 1=implementation strongest), a reality class (A IMPLEMENTED..G HYPOTHESIS/DOCUMENTED-ONLY), or a stable UNKNOWN/register reference; no B/C/G finding may be promoted to A, and documentation describing a desired behaviour is never itself evidence that the behaviour is implemented.

rows.anchor: No implementation changes (git status shows only study docs + bookkeeping). Implemented ≠ conceptual. EKS read-only; the commit diff on the baseline shows append/erratum only (no rewrite of §1–§20). Output marked PROPOSED · EVIDENCE-BASED · NON-AUTHORITATIVE · NOT ADOPTED.
rows.statement: Verification requirements (plan §9 DoD subset): no implementation changes may occur (git status shows only study docs and bookkeeping); implemented must not be conflated with conceptual; the EKS baseline diff must show append/erratum only, never a rewrite of §1-20; the output must be marked PROPOSED · EVIDENCE-BASED · NON-AUTHORITATIVE · NOT ADOPTED; the quarantined Review Set must never be used as current architecture.

rows.anchor: If the session terminates before commit/bookkeeping, the reviewing session completes bookkeeping and records the anomaly transparently — the deliverable text is never altered by the reviewing session.
rows.statement: Bookkeeping continuity rule: if a session terminates before completing commit and bookkeeping, a later reviewing session must complete the bookkeeping and transparently record the anomaly, but must never itself alter the deliverable text produced by the interrupted session.

rows.anchor: EKS has no runtime. It has mechanisms. There is no EKS service, daemon, scheduler, queue, database, or deployment unit. Every EKS behaviour is a command-line program that a human or an AI process chooses to invoke, plus a set of files in the repository.
rows.statement: Single most important structural finding of the baseline: EKS has no runtime, only mechanisms -- no service, daemon, scheduler, queue, database, or deployment unit exists; every EKS behaviour is a CLI program invoked by a human or AI process plus a set of repository files, and nothing in EKS runs unless something outside it runs it.

rows.anchor: The two EKS subsystems have inverse operational vitality, and the more valuable one is the less durable one. ... The subsystem that carries authority, ownership, and lineage for every governed engineering act writes to an untracked local directory. The subsystem that carries advisory code metrics writes to git.
rows.statement: Third major finding, first-hand and not stated in any prior document: the Governance/Workflow subsystem (last active 2026-08-21, gitignored, 29 tests, no CI gate) and the Observation/Assurance subsystem (last active 2026-08-04, git-tracked, 43+252 tests, one non-blocking CI gate) have inverse operational vitality -- the subsystem carrying authority/ownership/lineage is untracked, while the subsystem carrying advisory metrics is durably persisted.

rows.anchor: Answer to the joining-architect test ... Yes for the mechanisms, No for the domain. ... EKS's conceptual model is more mature than its executable boundaries, and its executable mechanisms are more mature than its domain model. Both statements are true simultaneously
rows.statement: Summary verdict of the whole baseline: a joining Principal Architect could understand EKS's mechanisms (sections 8-11, 15-16) precisely enough to run and extend them, but not its domain (sections 6-7, 9 show unmodelled language, unassigned invariant ownership, and only-candidate boundaries) -- 'EKS's conceptual model is more mature than its executable boundaries, and its executable mechanisms are more mature than its domain model,' both true simultaneously.

rows.anchor: To make engineering work on a multi-actor (human + AI) codebase adjudicable after the fact — so that any past engineering act can be traced to the authority that permitted it and the evidence that justified it. ... class B (implemented but implicit)
rows.statement: An inferred (class B, implemented-but-implicit) purpose is proposed for EKS, stated by no document itself: to make multi-actor (human+AI) engineering work adjudicable after the fact, so any past act can be traced to the authority that permitted it and the evidence that justified it -- explicitly labelled as an inference, not a finding.

assumptions.statement: every EKS mechanism serves this inferred purpose
assumptions.anchor: every mechanism serves it, and no artifact names it as the purpose

rows.anchor: not a database-backed system ... not event-driven ... not a service mesh / microservices ... not a deployment unit ... not continuously running ... not enforcing
rows.statement: EKS is verified-by-absence to be: not database-backed (zero PDO/mysqli/pg_connect/neo4j/elasticsearch/qdrant/weaviate hits), not event-driven (no bus/broker/queue/publisher/subscriber/event store), not a service mesh/microservices (no HTTP server/API surface/network call), not a deployment unit (no Dockerfile/manifest/CI deploy job), not continuously running (no git hooks installed), and not enforcing (0 locks, 0 leases, 0 blocking gates).

rows.anchor: EKS is not a separable system. It shares: the same git repository ... the same composer.json autoload ... the same phpunit.xml ... the same vendor/ ... the same CI runner ... the same .gitignore. Reuse in a second repository is therefore not demonstrated
rows.statement: EKS is not a separable system: it shares the same git repository, composer.json autoload namespace, phpunit.xml suite, vendor/, CI runner/workflows directory, and .gitignore with the PublicDigit product -- so EKS cannot be versioned, released, branched, or depended-on independently, and its durability is decided by a product config file; 'reuse in a second repository is therefore not demonstrated and, in the current shape, not possible without extraction' (class D, recorded not remedied).

rows.anchor: Operational state — first-hand, measured this session ... The observation/assurance loop has produced nothing for 17 days. The governance/workflow loop has run daily. Both are class-A implemented. Only one is in use.
rows.statement: Measured operational state: six observation/assurance streams (lcom4, recommendations, outcomes, assessments, watch-usage, test-presence.jsonl) last recorded activity 2026-08-03/04, dormant 17-18 days; the governance/workflow runtime and session logs were active the same day (2026-08-21). 'The subsystem that is durably persisted is the one that is dormant; the subsystem that is untracked is the one that is alive' (proposition P-6).

rows.anchor: EKS has no deployment. No Dockerfile, no image, no manifest, no service definition, no deploy job, no environment, no configuration management, no versioning, no release artifact. EKS 'deploys' by being present in a git checkout.
rows.statement: EKS has no deployment at all -- no Dockerfile, image, manifest, service definition, deploy job, environment, configuration management, versioning, or release artifact; it exists on exactly one developer workstation as one authoritative governance-state instance, local/untracked/unreplicated/unbackuped; both workflow assets are deliberately ON_DEMAND rather than SESSION_START, pending resolution of gap V-3.

rows.anchor: ⭐ COMPLETION 2026-08-22 (R-2) — U-18 CLOSED, the list is RECOVERED, not reconstructed. ... it is stated verbatim in the P1 execution commission ... Lesson recorded: 'absent from the corpus' is not the same as 'unknowable' — the commission that produced an artifact is itself evidence about that artifact.
rows.statement: U-18 (the special-question list, previously recorded UNKNOWN because it is 'not preserved anywhere in the corpus') is CLOSED, not by inference but by recovery: the list is stated verbatim in the P1 execution commission that produced §1-20, itself a text outside the corpus but evidence about the corpus. Lesson recorded: '"absent from the corpus" is not the same as "unknowable" — the commission that produced an artifact is itself evidence about that artifact.'

rows.anchor: ⭐ The strengths have a single common shape ... every one of them is a place where EKS made a guarantee structural instead of stated ... Where EKS is strong, it is because a rule was made impossible to break rather than important to follow. Where EKS is weak (§22, §23), the rule is stated and unenforced.
rows.statement: The 15 recorded Architectural Strengths (S-1..S-15, e.g. refusal/ambiguity/UNKNOWN as first-class tested outcomes; state always the fold of an append-only log; 324 green tests; contract tests asserting behaviour never implementation shape; structural rather than promissory guarantees; single interpretation authority with honest refusal; independent re-implementation as specification assurance; authority separated from lifecycle by construction; recommendation≠decision≠outcome≠assessment; repeated self-disclosure against interest; absence never implies permission; rules-as-data; genuine hexagonal discipline; self-measured non-use) share one shape: 'every one of them is a place where EKS made a guarantee structural instead of stated... where EKS is strong, it is because a rule was made impossible to break rather than important to follow. Where EKS is weak, the rule is stated and unenforced.'

rows.anchor: S-10 | Repeated, specific self-disclosure against interest | KOS_MECHANISM_PATH documented as 'NOT a hardened boundary...' · V-3 recorded as an open gap at qualification, remedy 'deliberately not chosen' · a registry verified.method correcting its own earlier miscount (F-2) ... an ADR binding its own producing process out of approving it
rows.statement: Strength S-10, 'repeated, specific self-disclosure against interest': examples include KOS_MECHANISM_PATH being documented as explicitly not a hardened boundary; gap V-3 recorded as open at the moment of qualification with its remedy 'deliberately not chosen'; a registry verified.method entry (AST-015) correcting its own earlier miscount (F-2) and admitting an authoring-order claim is 'recorded as unproven'; and a durability ADR binding its own producing process out of approving it.

rows.anchor: Maturity by layer ... Contract discipline ★★★★★ ... Governance tactical model (types, aggregates, VOs) ★☆☆☆☆ ... Persistence / durability ★☆☆☆☆ ... Temporal model ★☆☆☆☆ ... Separability / reuse ★☆☆☆☆ ... 1. Everything EKS knows is in files; everything EKS decides is recomputed from those files; and the most important of those files are not in git.
rows.statement: Closing maturity-by-layer assessment: contract discipline, deterministic-assurance implementation, and honesty of self-description all rate 5/5 stars; governance conceptual model (documented) rates 4/5 but unratified; governance tactical model, persistence/durability, temporal model, and separability/reuse all rate 1/5. The three sentences a joining Principal Architect most needs: (1) everything EKS knows is in files, everything it decides is recomputed from those files, and the most important files are not in git; (2) EKS refuses illegal writes to its own record and prevents nothing else -- its authority is evidentiary, not operative, by recorded design; (3) where EKS has invariants it has no types, and where it has types it has no authority -- so folder-structure boundaries are not the boundaries the invariants imply.

sources.note: Disciplined reformulation of the Yoni metaphor as a research lens (not a kernel definition), with a formal Yoni Epistemic Field Y_t distinct from K_t, six falsifiable hypotheses (YL-H1..H6), and a three-layer [EXT]/[PROP]/[EXP] provenance discipline; culminates the corrective sequence begun in the four-conflations critique.

rows.anchor: We should not define: Kernel = Yoni. Instead: Yoni Lens → a way of viewing the epistemic system. The lens asks: What kind of epistemic field must exist for knowledge to be generated, challenged, transformed and renewed?
rows.statement: Reframes the Yoni Lens as a way of viewing the epistemic system (not a kernel definition), asking what kind of epistemic field must exist for knowledge to be generated, challenged, transformed, and renewed.

rows.anchor: Y_t = Yoni Epistemic Field ... Y_t = (K_t, Q_t, E_t, H_t, A_t, C_t, S_t) ... not necessarily the final mathematical definition ... Y_t ≠ K_t and Y_t ≠ 𝒦. The field contains and relates things that the kernel operates upon.
rows.statement: Defines the candidate Yoni Epistemic Field Y_t=(K_t,Q_t,E_t,H_t,A_t,C_t,S_t) (knowledge state, inquiry, evidence, hypotheses, arguments, context, standards), explicitly Y_t != K_t and Y_t != Kernel -- the field contains and relates what the kernel operates upon.

rows.anchor: P_t(H)=case supporting H, N_t(H)=case challenging H. Then: A_t(H)=P_t(H)∪N_t(H) is the Argument Field ... But crucially: P_t + N_t = 0 must not mean knowledge. ... So the Yoni Lens gives us polarity, but not a scalar algebra.
rows.statement: Defines epistemic polarity via P_t(H) (supporting case) and N_t(H) (challenging case) union-composed into the Argument Field A_t(H), explicitly rejecting P_t+N_t=0 as meaning knowledge (per the closure experiment's ten non-equivalent zero-sum conditions) -- polarity without scalar algebra.

rows.anchor: I think we should abandon that [scalar +n+(-n)=0] as a theoretical mechanism. The deeper idea is: Difference creates a relational field. ... INQUIRY -> PROPOSAL/CHALLENGE -> ARGUMENT FIELD -> SUPPORT/DEFEAT/CONFLICT -> EVIDENCE ASSESSMENT -> RECONCILIATION? -> NO:REVISION / YES:CLOSURE EVENT -> NEW EPISTEMIC STATE.
rows.statement: Abandons the scalar +n+(-n)=0 mechanism entirely in favor of 'difference creates a relational field', giving a revised non-scalar pipeline diagram: Inquiry->{Proposal,Challenge}->ArgumentField->{Support,Defeat,Conflict}->EvidenceAssessment->Reconciliation?->(No:Revision / Yes:ClosureEvent)->NewEpistemicState.

rows.anchor: K_{t+1} = Θ(K_t, Q_t, E_t, A_t, S_t, M_t, C_t) could be viewed through the Yoni Lens as: the emergence of a new epistemic configuration from interaction within the field. ... It does not establish that the equation is mathematically derived from the Yoni metaphor.
rows.statement: Offers the Yoni Lens as a philosophical interpretation (not a mathematical derivation) of the existing transition equation K_{t+1}=Theta(K_t,Q_t,E_t,A_t,S_t,M_t,C_t): the emergence of a new epistemic configuration from interaction within the field.

rows.anchor: K_{t+1} → ZeroLens → Boundary → Inquiry → Interaction → K_{t+2}. Therefore: Generation → Examination → Regeneration. The field is therefore recursively generative. ... Zero does not mean 'There is nothing left.' Rather: 'Examine what this newly generated state still does not represent.'
rows.statement: Formalizes the recursive Generation->Examination->Regeneration cycle (K_{t+1}->ZeroLens->Boundary->Inquiry->Interaction->K_{t+2}), clarifying Zero does not mean 'nothing left' but 'examine what this newly generated state still does not represent' -- combining Yoni Lens (generative field) with Zero Lens (boundary examination).

rows.anchor: Layer Y1 - [EXT] Philosophical source/metaphor ... Layer Y2 - [PROP] KnowledgeOS interpretation ... Layer Y3 - [EXP] Empirical correspondence: We test whether the proposed lens actually illuminates structures already independently discovered ... If it predicts nothing new and merely renames existing concepts, its theoretical value is limited.
rows.statement: Establishes a three-layer provenance discipline for the Yoni Lens: Y1 [EXT] the raw philosophical source/metaphor; Y2 [PROP] the KnowledgeOS interpretation (Difference->Interaction->Assessment->Transformation->Emergence); Y3 [EXP] empirical correspondence testing whether the lens illuminates independently-discovered structures (Proposal/Challenge, Argument Field, Evidence Assessment, Reconciliation, Closure Event, Zero Lens, recursive inquiry) -- if it only renames existing concepts, its theoretical value is limited.

rows.anchor: Does the Yoni Lens reveal a structural property of epistemic systems that is not adequately visible through the current KnowledgeOS model? ... YL-H1 Relationality ... YL-H2 Generativity ... YL-H3 Polarity ... YL-H4 Non-collapse ... YL-H5 Recursion ... YL-H6 Role plurality.
rows.statement: Reframes the research question from 'can Yoni define the kernel' to 'does the Yoni Lens reveal a structural property not adequately visible through the current model', and states six independently-testable hypotheses: YL-H1 Relationality (transformation requires relations among differentiated contributions), YL-H2 Generativity (a state can produce a configuration not simply stored beforehand), YL-H3 Polarity (inquiry benefits from representing both support and challenge), YL-H4 Non-collapse (opposition/support cannot safely reduce to scalar cancellation), YL-H5 Recursion (a generated state becomes the field for subsequent boundary examination), YL-H6 Role plurality (epistemic poles are roles, not persons/components).

rows.anchor: Yoni = Relational Potentiality. Not 'the womb of knowledge.' Not 'the kernel.' Not 'Zero.' Rather: the space of possible epistemic interactions from which a subsequent epistemic configuration may emerge. ... Potential Field ≠ Current State.
rows.statement: Proposes the strongest candidate reading: Yoni = Relational Potentiality, the space of possible epistemic interactions (relations, hypotheses, challenges, interpretations, evidence interactions) from which a subsequent configuration may emerge, distinct from K_t (the currently realized state) -- Potential Field != Current State.

rows.anchor: Yoni Lens Hypothesis. The Yoni Lens interprets an epistemic system as a receptive, relational and generative field ... The lens does not identify this field with the KnowledgeOS kernel, Zero, truth, determination or knowledge. Its central structural hypothesis is that epistemic emergence can be understood as difference → interaction → assessment → transformation → new epistemic state, followed recursively by boundary examination and further inquiry.
rows.statement: States the canonical [PROP] 'Yoni Lens Hypothesis': an epistemic system as a receptive/relational/generative field where differentiated contributions interact and transform the current state, explicitly not identified with the kernel, Zero, truth, determination, or knowledge; central structural claim is difference->interaction->assessment->transformation->new-state, recursively followed by boundary examination and further inquiry.

rows.anchor: The next rigorous step would be a Yoni Lens Theory Specification + falsification experiment: derive the lens's necessary primitives from the metaphor, map each to existing KnowledgeOS constructs, identify genuinely new predictions, and then test whether the lens adds explanatory power or merely renames Proposal/Challenge/Argument/Assessment/Closure.
rows.statement: Proposes the concrete next step: a Yoni Lens Theory Specification plus falsification experiment deriving necessary primitives, mapping them to existing constructs, identifying genuinely new predictions, and testing whether the lens adds explanatory power beyond renaming Proposal/Challenge/Argument/Assessment/Closure.

rows.anchor: Date: 2026-09-02. Status: [PROP] -- Research Formulation. Authority: HPA Supervisory. Predecessor: Sexual-Epistemic Metaphor Simulations. Purpose: Formalize the Yoni Lens as a philosophical/epistemological lens over KnowledgeOS, distinct from the kernel definition.
rows.statement: A formal specification document dated 2026-09-02, issued under 'HPA Supervisory' authority, explicitly naming its predecessor as the 'Sexual-Epistemic Metaphor Simulations' track and its purpose as formalizing the Yoni Lens as a lens distinct from the kernel definition -- consolidating S2448/S2449 into governed specification form.

rows.statement: Proposes an explicit DDD concept-mapping table for the Yoni Lens: Field->Bounded Context (Knowledge Context), Proposal->Command (Assert), Challenge->Command (Refute), Argument->Domain Event (Evidence Assessment), Assessment->Domain Service (EvidenceAggregator), Offspring->Aggregate (KnowledgeState) -- the lens explicitly is not itself an aggregate ('YoniAggregate' is rejected).

rows.anchor: | Hypothesis | Falsification | | YL-H1 | Evidence of transformation without relations | | YL-H2 | All new states are pre-stored | | YL-H3 | No benefit from explicit polarity | | YL-H4 | Scalar cancellation is sufficient | | YL-H5 | No recursive cycle | | YL-H6 | Roles are fixed to persons |
rows.statement: Specifies an explicit falsification condition for each of the six YL hypotheses: YL-H1 falsified by transformation-without-relations evidence, YL-H2 by all-new-states-pre-stored, YL-H3 by no-benefit-from-explicit-polarity, YL-H4 by scalar-cancellation-being-sufficient, YL-H5 by no-recursive-cycle, YL-H6 by roles-being-fixed-to-persons -- turning the six hypotheses into a testable protocol.

rows.statement: Final status table: the Yoni Lens formulation, its six hypotheses, and its three-layer structure are all [PROP]; empirical testing is [EXP] PENDING; canonical adoption is explicitly NOT YET.

rows.anchor: The Yoni Lens and Zero Lens are complementary, not competing. They represent two phases of a single epistemic cycle: Yoni Lens | Generation | 'What can emerge?' ... Zero Lens | Examination | 'What is not yet established?' ... Yoni → Generates → State → Zero → Examines → Boundary → Inquiry → Yoni.
rows.statement: Proposes the Yoni Lens (generation, 'what can emerge?') and Zero Lens (examination, 'what is not yet established?') as complementary phases of a single epistemic cycle rather than competing formulations, forming a candidate complete epistemic engine.

rows.anchor: Yoni without Zero = Blind generation. Zero without Yoni = Sterile examination. Yoni × Zero = Generative examination.
rows.statement: Argues the two lenses are individually incomplete: Yoni without Zero produces blind generation (no self-critique), Zero without Yoni produces sterile examination (nothing to examine or renew), while their combination is generative examination.

rows.anchor: 𝒰_t = Unified Epistemic Field = 𝒴_t ∪ 𝒵_t ... 𝒰_t = (K_t, Q_t, E_t, H_t, A_t, C_t, S_t, B_t, G_t, Δ_t) ... K_t Kernel, B_t Boundary (Zero findings), G_t Gaps, Δ_t Discrepancy.
rows.statement: Defines a ten-component Unified Epistemic Field U_t=(K_t,Q_t,E_t,H_t,A_t,C_t,S_t,B_t,G_t,Delta_t), merging the Yoni Lens's seven-component field with three Zero-Lens-derived components (Boundary, Gaps, Discrepancy).

rows.anchor: | | Yoni Generative | Yoni Not Generative | | Zero Examining | Healthy Epistemic Cycle | Sterile Examination | | Zero Not Examining | Blind Generation | Stagnation |
rows.statement: Proposes a 2x2 generativity-examination matrix over {Yoni Generative/Not} x {Zero Examining/Not}, yielding four states: Healthy Epistemic Cycle, Sterile Examination, Blind Generation, and Stagnation.

rows.anchor: K_{t+2} = Zero(Yoni(K_t, Q_t, E_t, A_t, S_t, C_t)) ... YZ(K_t, Q_t, E_t, A_t, S_t, C_t) = (K_{t+1}, B_t, G_t, Δ_t) ... // Yoni Phase ... // Kernel Phase ... // Zero Phase ... // Reconciliation Phase ... return (K_next, B_next, G_next, Δ_next)
rows.statement: Specifies a combined transition function K_{t+2}=Zero(Yoni(K_t,Q_t,E_t,A_t,S_t,C_t)) and a concrete YZ() algorithm with four phases (Yoni: generate hypotheses/form proposals; Kernel: apply transitions; Zero: examine boundary/detect gaps/detect conflicts; Reconciliation: reconcile and compute discrepancy), producing (K_next, B_next, G_next, Delta_next) -- this is the concrete algorithm executed in the following N-yoni-zero-lens-cycle-test file.

experiment.hypothesis: A combined generation-then-examination cycle (Yoni then Zero) forms a complete epistemic engine
experiment.setup: K_t, Q_t, E_t, A_t, S_t, C_t as inputs to a four-phase YZ() pipeline
experiment.assumptions: unstated
experiment.inputs: as above
experiment.method: Generate_Hypotheses -> Form_Proposals -> Apply_Transitions -> Examine_Boundary -> Detect_Gaps/Conflicts -> Reconcile -> Compute_Discrepancy

rows.anchor: The Yoni-Zero cycle is not a circle. It is a spiral: Level 3: Transformed knowledge ... Level 0: Initial state. Each cycle deepens understanding. ... Yoni-Zero cycle never terminates. Because: Each new state creates new boundaries; each boundary creates new inquiry; each inquiry creates new generation.
rows.statement: Proposes the cycle is a spiral rather than a circle (each iteration deepens understanding rather than repeating identically) and a non-termination principle: the Yoni-Zero cycle never terminates because each new state creates new boundaries, which create new inquiry, which creates new generation.

rows.anchor: Yoni Lens | Generation | Creates new states ... Zero Lens | Examination | Detects boundaries ... Lord Lens | Candidate generation | Sub-function of Yoni ... Sārathi Lens | Guidance | Uses Zero output. ... KnowledgeOS = Yoni ∘ Zero ∘ Sārathi.
rows.statement: Integrates the Lord and Sarathi lenses into the Yoni-Zero framework as a lens hierarchy (Lord Lens as a sub-function of Yoni for candidate generation; Sarathi Lens using Zero's output for guidance), proposing the composed function KnowledgeOS = Yoni-compose-Zero-compose-Sarathi.
