rows.statement: Replay is conditionally computable under six named preconditions, and is proven to REQUIRE operation versioning (since changing an operation's semantics between (T1^2026) and (T1^2027) could replay the same history to different states, replayability implies immutable-or-versioned transformation semantics); Replay is also proven distinct from Reversal — if T is many-to-one (K1!=K2 but T(K1)=T(K2)), no inverse can uniquely reconstruct the original state, so Replay only reconstructs the forward computation, it does not recover an original state from an output.

rows.statement: Derives that replay requires preserving policy version identity (since a later policy change could make replay reproduce a different result), but explicitly resists the inference that Policy therefore belongs in K — History can instead retain a PolicyRef, consistent with the general principle that whatever affects what the next state IS belongs to T, while whatever affects only who/when belongs to History.

rows.anchor: CONSTITUTIONAL KERNEL <- the eleven articles (PRESERVE) ... Engine Layer (GOVERN) ... Mechanisms (GOVERN) ... Representations (ENABLE) ... Implementation (ENABLE)
rows.statement: Chapter III, the Kernel Boundary: a 5-tier diagram -- Constitutional Kernel (the 11 articles, PRESERVE) served by Engine Layer (validation engines, fallacy detection, debate pipeline, intent classification, verdict vocabulary, GOVERN), Mechanisms (epistemic-inquiry lifecycle, reasoning pipelines, GOVERN), Representations (evidence records, context tuples, epistemic state model, absence taxonomy, epistemic graph, typed encodings, ENABLE), and Implementation (storage, interfaces, systems, deliberately unconstrained, ENABLE). III.1 the kernel does not do the reasoning -- it states what must be preserved/never collapse; engines execute governed transformations realizing those constraints. III.2 no engine/mechanism/representation may violate an article -- evolution that violates an article is a corruption, not an evolution, subject to Chapter V. III.3 implementation is deliberately out of constitutional scope.

rows.anchor: V.1 Engineering evolution -- no amendment required. ... V.2 Constitutional amendment -- required ... V.3 What amendment MAY do ... V.4 Ratification.
rows.statement: Chapter V, Amendment Discipline (new content, not present verbatim in any prior artifact in this file group): engines/mechanisms/representations/implementation (Chapter III) MAY evolve freely provided no evolution violates an article (V.1); the 11 articles, the character, the negative boundary, and the kernel/engine boundary SHALL NOT change except by HPA-ratified constitutional amendment, and no article SHALL be weakened (V.2); amendment MAY refine wording, correct inconsistency, or -- on evidence a specific corruption is unguarded -- add a strengthening clause, but SHALL NOT add new concepts/sources/rows ('the corpus that produced this Constitution is closed; adding knowledge to the kernel would violate the discipline this Constitution establishes', V.3); amendment is effective only by HPA ruling following the same evidence/domain-independence/necessity/failure-test discipline that produced step 5 (V.4).

rows.anchor: L1 — the constitutional layer
rows.statement: Describes L1 as eleven articles (Identity, Dimension, Authority, Decision, Projection, Verification, Failure-State, Contradiction, Unknown, Agency, History), each a negation forbidding a specific epistemic collapse; states the articles are boundary laws stating what must never happen, not how anything works; their ratification is carried by the retrospective ratification act of 2026-08-22 (GN-27 resolution of finding CF-003).

rows.anchor: Convergence across traditions
rows.statement: The constitutional layer arrived at the same prohibition from a different direction: a 'knowledge quality' scalar is a forbidden surrogate (Article 2's failure signature is literally 'Knowledge Quality = 0.87'). One prohibition, two independent derivations -- treated as evidence, while still refusing to call it proof.

rows.anchor: The constitutional layer's Chapter V parallel
rows.statement: The constitutional layer's Chapter V is the same idea in constitutional form: engineering evolution free below the articles; amendment of the articles only by ratified act; no weakening. Two traditions, one stratification, arrived at independently.

rows.anchor: The constitutional kernel
rows.statement: The eleven articles, selected from twenty-nine registered rows by an explicit human ruling and formalized as the constitution -- fewer laws, not fewer truths. Its identity is prohibitive: each article forbids a named collapse, and each was failure-tested (remove it, and a named corruption opens). This kernel governs; it does not compute.

aliases: Guna as mode/state model, not metaphysics

single_candidate_flags.why_uncertain: Proposes the same guna-as-operating-mode idea (M_t in {Sattva,Rajas,Tamas}) as the B0054 guna-mode-conditioned-state-machine-hypothesis; may be an early seed of that same object rather than a new one.

sources.note: Reformulates guna (Sattva/Rajas/Tamas) explicitly as a MODE/STATE model (not Gita metaphysics): K_t=(X_t,M_t) with M_t in {S,R,T} a control/state variable governing which kernel operators are admissible (O_S, O_R, O_T subset O), rather than a fourth Sigma dimension. Gives mode-specific operator sets (O_S={Observe,Compare,Discriminate,Corroborate,Qualify,Resolve,Validate}; O_R={Search,Acquire,Transform,Investigate,Generate,Execute}; O_T={DetectBlock,ExposeUnknown,Suspend,Flag,Invalidate,RequestEvidence}), a mode-sensitive Buddhi discriminator B_t:(E_t,K_t,M_t)->{accept,reject,investigate,suspend,transform} (same evidence yields different actions per mode), and a Tamas->Zero->Buddhi->Sattva mode-transition hypothesis. Explicitly distinguishes this from the earlier per-chapter guna-conditioning-regime object by treating mode as a control variable rather than a fourth Sigma dimension, and poses a 10-question research checklist (can S/R/T be defined without theology, can modes be detected computationally, is mode another axis or a control variable over axes, etc).

The Guna-as-kernel-operating-mode hypothesis, first proposed in B0054 and substantially extended in B0055 (mode-dependent Buddhi, an independent mode state machine, later reframed as a falsifiable experimental control variable).

rows.anchor: K_t=(X_t,M_t) ... a state machine with mode-dependent transition semantics
rows.statement: Rejects modeling Sattva/Rajas/Tamas as three separate kernels K_S,K_R,K_T; instead K_t=(X_t,M_t) where X_t is the knowledge/epistemic state and M_t in {S,R,T} the current operational mode, with K_t --O_{M_t}--> K_{t+1} and the mode itself able to change M_t->M_{t+1}, giving K_{t+1}=T(K_t,o_t,M_t) -- a state machine with mode-dependent transition semantics.

rows.anchor: O_S=\{Observe,Compare,Discriminate,Corroborate,Qualify,Resolve,Validate\} ... O_R=\{Search,Acquire,Transform,Investigate,Generate,Execute\} ... O_T=\{DetectBlock,ExposeUnknown,Suspend,Flag,Invalidate,RequestEvidence\}
rows.statement: Proposes mode-dependent admissible operator sets O_{M_t} subset O = full operator set: O_S (Sattva, clarification/discrimination mode) = {Observe,Compare,Discriminate,Corroborate,Qualify,Resolve,Validate}; O_R (Rajas, activity/acquisition mode) = {Search,Acquire,Transform,Investigate,Generate,Execute}; O_T (Tamas, obscuration mode) = diagnostic operators {DetectBlock,ExposeUnknown,Suspend,Flag,Invalidate,RequestEvidence}, not productive operators. Warns Rajas is not inherently bad (a system with zero Rajas would never investigate anything); the problem is uncontrolled Rajas (activity does not imply knowledge) -- 'more operations do not necessarily produce more knowledge'.

rows.anchor: T \xrightarrow{\text{Detect ignorance}} Zero \xrightarrow{\text{Buddhi}} S
rows.statement: Connects Tamas to Zero: Zero -> representation/detection of epistemic absence; Tamas can trigger a transition toward Sattva via: T --Detect ignorance--> Zero --Buddhi--> S -- proposed as a very interesting mode-transition hypothesis.

rows.anchor: B_t: (E_t,K_t,M_t) \rightarrow \{\text{accept},\text{reject},\text{investigate},\text{suspend},\text{transform}\} ... DO NOTHING ... is itself a Buddhi decision.
rows.statement: Formalizes Buddhi as mode-sensitive: B_t:(E_t,K_t,M_t)->{accept,reject,investigate,suspend,transform}. The same evidence E can lead to different actions depending on mode: in Sattva, E->B_S->investigate carefully; in Rajas, E->B_R->act/acquire immediately; in Tamas, E->B_T->ignore/suspend/block. Refines the earlier 'kernel always busy determining right and wrong' into: the kernel continuously evaluates the epistemic condition of its current state and determines which transitions are admissible under its current operational mode; a kernel may legitimately decide DO NOTHING because evidence is insufficient, and that itself is a Buddhi decision.

lineage_claims.target: 'kernel always busy determining right and wrong' statement
lineage_claims.quote: I would refine that.

rows.anchor: Guṇa mode is NOT another knowledge dimension ... Guṇa mode = a control/state variable governing how the kernel operates on knowledge
rows.statement: Central hypothesis: Guna mode is NOT another knowledge dimension (i.e. not a sixth axis of Sigma); rather Guna mode = a control/state variable governing how the kernel operates on knowledge -- assessed as potentially much cleaner than adding another dimension to Sigma=(A,S,R,V,C). Proposes next research direction: derive a formal Kernel Operator Algebra from the combined Chapters 6-17 model with Buddhi as discriminator and Sattva/Rajas/Tamas as candidate operational modes, without canonizing Gita terminology.
missing: derivation confirming mode is control-variable not axis

rows.anchor: Can S,R,T be defined without relying on Sanskrit theology? ... Is mode another axis, or is it a control variable over the axes?
rows.statement: Poses a 10-question research checklist for the Mode-Conditioned Epistemic State Machine hypothesis: can S,R,T be defined without Sanskrit theology; can each mode be given measurable properties; are modes mutually exclusive, overlapping, or mixtures; can a kernel transition between modes; does every operator have a mode-dependent admissibility condition; can a Tamas-like state be detected computationally; can Buddhi be represented as an actual decision function; does this improve the existing Sigma=(A,S,R,V,C) model; is mode another axis or a control variable over the axes; can the resulting algebra be independently derived from KnowledgeOS requirements (marked as the crucial distinction).

rows.anchor: Is "epistemic quality" actually a sixth dimension? ... If those five dimensions already capture the relevant distinctions, then Q\notin\Sigma
rows.statement: Proposes a concrete falsifiability test for whether guna/quality is a sixth Sigma dimension: check each existing axis against the candidate quality distinctions -- Acquisition (was knowledge acquired via identifiable observation), State (is epistemic state appropriately represented), Relation (are relationships correctly represented), Verification/Validation (is evidence sufficient), Context (is interpretation appropriate to context). If the five axes already capture the relevant distinctions, then Q notin Sigma (quality is a derived property); if they cannot, that is evidence for a missing dimension -- explicitly framed as the mathematical discipline wanted, before adding a sixth axis.
missing: the actual test execution and result

experiment.hypothesis: Epistemic quality/guna-like distinctions are already representable within the existing five-axis Sigma, so no sixth dimension is needed.
experiment.setup: For each of the five Sigma axes, check whether it already captures the relevant guna-related distinction.
experiment.assumptions: The five axes as currently defined are exhaustive of what they claim to cover.
experiment.inputs: Definitions of Acquisition, State, Relation, Verification, Context axes.
experiment.method: Map each candidate quality distinction (clarity, activity/attachment, obscuration) onto the five axes and check coverage.
experiment.result: Not executed in this file; proposed only.
experiment.interpretation: If covered, quality is derived (Q notin Sigma); if not, evidence for a missing dimension.
experiment.limitations: Requires precise axis definitions to execute rigorously.
experiment.conclusion: Proposed as the next falsification step, not yet run.

rows.anchor: \operatorname{Distortion}(K_t)\rightarrow 0 ... M may be a derived property of (K,B,Z,\delta,\Sigma,C)
rows.statement: Rejects Moksha=maximum knowledge and Moksha=|K|->infinity; proposes instead Moksha ~ a limiting condition of epistemic purification, potentially Distortion(K_t)->0, explicitly a research hypothesis not an established theorem. Proposes candidate minimal kernel M=(K,B,Z,delta,Sigma) and states the current mathematical/DDD expectation: mode M={Sattva,Rajas,Tamas} may be a DERIVED property of (K,B,Z,delta,Sigma,C) rather than an additional primitive component -- explicitly framed as the kind of result wanted from the Gita programme (force every proposed concept through typing, independence, falsification, minimality, DDD boundaries). Proposes composed transition K_{t+1}=delta(K_t,x_t,B_t,M_t,C_t) as a hypothesis pending this determination.
missing: determination of whether M_t is derived or primitive

rows.anchor: S,R,T=\text{different modes of operation} ... Rajas \rightarrow useful acquisition ... Sattva \rightarrow incorrect conclusion
rows.statement: Explicit correction against a crude reading: NOT Sattva=good knowledge, Rajas=bad knowledge, Tamas=bad knowledge. Instead S,R,T = different modes of operation (operational tendencies, not truth labels); the quality of resulting knowledge is evaluated separately. Concrete counterexamples: Rajas -> useful acquisition is possible; Sattva -> incorrect conclusion is possible if underlying evidence/model is defective; Tamas can produce a legitimate stop (insufficient evidence -> do not act).
invariants: modes are operational tendencies, not truth labels

rows.anchor: Knowledge State \neq Kernel State ... A kernel can contain excellent knowledge while operating in a poor mode.
rows.statement: Explicit separation: Knowledge State K_t answers 'what does the system currently represent/know', Kernel State (fraktur K)_t = (K_t,M_t,B_t,Z_t,Pi_t) answers 'in what condition is the system currently processing that knowledge'. K_t != (fraktur K)_t: a kernel can contain excellent knowledge while operating in a poor mode, or hold incomplete knowledge with excellent discrimination/qualification behaviour -- assessed as very important for the Sattva/Rajas/Tamas model. Candidate kernel transition: (fraktur K)_t --Buddhi--> o_t --Purify--> (fraktur K)_{t+1}. Final consolidated formula: K_{t+1}=Purify(Execute(Buddhi(K_t,O_t,C_t))). Concluding principle: the Kernel is not the Knowledge; the Kernel is the smallest active unit that operates on Knowledge.

rows.anchor: Neither branch is free. The flag is not lifted — it is converted from a vague caution into a two-branch question with named costs.
rows.statement: Sharpens the Guna flag (open since REFINED-STEP-286 sec4, which required Guna to declare a scale type before being opened, touching the untyped Threshold/theta gap) into a two-branch fork P1': Branch 1, G_t derived from Sigma (e.g. mode=goodness when support is strong) -- the theta/scale-type gap returns, since a derivation rule over S's ordinal bands is exactly what sec4 flagged; Branch 2, G_t independent of Sigma -- a new state component with no carrier, and K_t=(Sigma_t,G_t,...) becomes another open-ended tuple that 258.35 warns against. Neither branch is free; sec4's gate still binds since neither branch declares a scale type. Contrasts with external_research mapping Guna->Sigma directly, which artifact 19's E2 finding already showed produces a type error.
missing: resolution of the fork

rows.anchor: o_t = \Omega_{G_t} \left( B_t,K_t,Z_t \right)
rows.statement: Formalizes the guna mode as selecting an operator POLICY, not merely a descriptive label: o_t = Omega_{G_t}(B_t,K_t,Z_t), giving Tamas mode o=Ignore; Rajas mode o=Search->Act->Search; Sattva mode o=Discriminate->Qualify->(Act or Stop) -- illustrated on identical K_t and O_t across modes, giving 'different modes of mind -> different operators/behaviour' a formal shape.

lineage_claims.quote: This gives your idea a formal shape.

rows.anchor: Buddhi(K_t,Z_t,M_t) \rightarrow D_t ... Unrecognized ignorance
rows.statement: Extends Buddhi to include the operating mode: Buddhi(K_t,Z_t,M_t)->D_t, giving 'the same Knowledge State can produce different processing trajectories depending on the kernel's operating mode' as a testable hypothesis. Tamas failure mode: kernel encounters Z_t not-empty but behaves as though Z_t=empty, producing unrecognized ignorance; Rajas failure mode: continuous action Action_1->Action_2->Action_3 without sufficient discrimination -- the kernel needs self-regulation, connecting Chapter 6's discipline material to kernel architecture rather than mere commentary.

rows.anchor: M_t in {Sattva,Rajas,Tamas} ... best treated initially as operating regimes, not new knowledge primitives ... Sattva: clarity, coherence, balance ... Rajas: activity, change, competition ... Tamas: inertia, ignorance, obscuration ... classified Guna as a quality/state heuristic rather than automatically putting it into the kernel.
rows.statement: Gunas -> kernel operating modes, M_t in {Sattva, Rajas, Tamas}, best treated initially as operating regimes rather than new knowledge primitives: Sattva (clarity, coherence, balance, discrimination, reliable evaluation), Rajas (activity, change, competition, action pressure, rapid transformation), Tamas (inertia, ignorance, obscuration, corruption, failure to discriminate). Earlier research is noted to have deliberately classified Guna as a quality/state heuristic rather than putting it directly into the kernel, and that caution is preserved here.

rows.anchor: B_{Sattva}(K) ... clear discrimination ... B_{Rajas}(K) ... action-biased interpretation ... B_{Tamas}(K) ... failure to recognize relevant evidence ... Decision = f(K,B,M,Gamma) rather than Decision = f(K) ... a major conceptual expansion of the Kernel model.
rows.statement: The same knowledge state K can behave differently under different operating modes: B_Sattva(K) may yield clear discrimination, B_Rajas(K) an action-biased interpretation, B_Tamas(K) a failure to recognize relevant evidence -- yielding Decision = f(K,B,M,Gamma) rather than Decision = f(K), described as a major conceptual expansion of the Kernel model.

rows.anchor: M_t in {Sattva,Rajas,Tamas} as modes of Kernel operation, not as permanent identities ... O_t = f(M_t,B_t,C_t) ... M_t -> M_{t+1} independently from K_t -> K_{t+1} ... Knowledge state and Kernel mode are different state dimensions ... high knowledge + poor mode ... little knowledge + high discrimination ... These are not equivalent.
rows.statement: Gunas modeled as Kernel operation modes (not permanent identities), M_t in {Sattva, Rajas, Tamas}, giving O_t = f(M_t,B_t,C_t) -- the same candidate operation can behave differently under different modes. Proposes an independent mode state machine M_t -> M_{t+1} running alongside the knowledge state machine K_t -> K_{t+1}: knowledge state and Kernel mode are different state dimensions, so 'high knowledge + poor mode' and 'little knowledge + high discrimination' are not equivalent conditions.

rows.anchor: G_t in {Sattva,Rajas,Tamas} ... B_{G_t}: K_t -> D_t ... mode-dependent operators, rather than treating the three Guṇas as static labels.
rows.statement: Models Sattva/Rajas/Tamas as G_t in {Sattva,Rajas,Tamas} sitting above the eight primitives, with mode-dependent Buddhi B_{G_t}: K_t -> D_t (Sattva: clarity/discrimination/consistency/evidence/balanced judgement; Rajas: activity/change/pursuit/intervention/rapid transformation; Tamas: inertia/ignorance/unresolved contradiction/refusal to inspect) -- emphasized as giving mode-dependent operators rather than static labels.

rows.anchor: G_t in {Sattva,Rajas,Tamas} ... B_G: K -> Op* where Op* is the set of admissible operations ... B_Sattva -> {verify, qualify, reconcile, discriminate} ... B_Rajas -> {act, transform, pursue, propagate} ... B_Tamas -> {defer, retain, expose uncertainty} ... These are hypotheses, not yet canonical operations. The mathematical operator itself remains well-defined.
rows.statement: Refines the Guna-mode hypothesis so mode influences which operators are admissible/preferred (B_G: K -> Op*, the set of admissible operations) without changing the operators' own mathematical definitions: B_Sattva -> {verify, qualify, reconcile, discriminate}; B_Rajas -> {act, transform, pursue, propagate}; B_Tamas -> {defer, retain, expose uncertainty} -- explicitly hypotheses, not yet canonical operations.

rows.anchor: G_t in {Sattva,Rajas,Tamas} ... O_i^(G) rather than assuming every operator behaves identically in every mode ... Tamas: concealment, stagnation, refusal to distinguish, failure to expose Zero ... Rajas: excessive transformation, action, acquisition, movement ... Sattva: discrimination, clarity, qualification, balanced transformation ... We should test whether these philosophical distinctions correspond to measurable operator behaviour. If not, they remain philosophical interpretation.
rows.statement: Reframes the three Guna modes as operator-selection hypotheses to be experimentally tested: G_t in {Sattva,Rajas,Tamas} gives mode-specific operator variants O_i^(G) rather than uniform behavior, with hypothesized tendencies (Tamas: concealment/stagnation/refusal to distinguish/failure to expose Zero; Rajas: excessive transformation/action/acquisition/movement; Sattva: discrimination/clarity/qualification/balanced transformation), and an explicit falsifiability condition: test whether these philosophical distinctions correspond to measurable operator behaviour; if not, they remain philosophical interpretation only.

rows.anchor: Remove G_t from the formal kernel state for now. G_t in {Sattva,Rajas,Tamas} and mode-dependent operators is an excellent experimental hypothesis. But it should sit in the PHILOSOPHICAL RESEARCH LAYER (Gītā -> Guṇa hypothesis -> measurable behavioural hypothesis -> experiment -> correspondence?) not in K_t=(...,G_t,...) until independently justified.
rows.statement: Removes G_t (Guna) from the formal kernel state, relegating it to an explicit philosophical research layer (Gita -> Guna hypothesis -> measurable behavioural hypothesis -> experiment -> correspondence?) rather than embedding it directly in K_t=(...,G_t,...) until independently justified -- an excellent experimental hypothesis, but not yet a kernel-state component.

rows.anchor: B_G: (K_t,O_t) -> (K_{t+1},E_t) where G is an experimental condition. Tamas-like mode: failure to expose contradictions? persistence of stale knowledge? failure to detect Zero? refusal to revise? Rajas-like mode: excessive transformations? premature action? uncontrolled acquisition? overproduction of hypotheses? Sattva-like mode: better discrimination? clearer qualification? stronger provenance? lower contradiction? more appropriate uncertainty? These become empirical experiments, not philosophical assertions.
rows.statement: Turns the Guna model into an experimental control variable: B_G: (K_t,O_t) -> (K_{t+1},E_t) with G as an experimental condition, and gives falsifiable per-mode empirical questions -- Tamas-like (failure to expose contradictions? persistence of stale knowledge? failure to detect Zero? refusal to revise?), Rajas-like (excessive transformations? premature action? uncontrolled acquisition? overproduction of hypotheses?), Sattva-like (better discrimination? clearer qualification? stronger provenance? lower contradiction? more appropriate uncertainty?) -- explicitly framed as empirical experiments, not philosophical assertions.

rows.anchor: Mode_t in {Sattva,Rajas,Tamas}. But what is the mathematical meaning? Mode(K_t) as: epistemic regime, transformation regime, uncertainty regime, decision bias, stability regime. We need measurable criteria. Otherwise Guṇa remains purely metaphorical. ... What is t? wall-clock time? observation sequence? version? event number? knowledge revision? logical time? KnowledgeOS probably needs event time/logical time in addition to physical time. Potentially K^(n) may actually be more appropriate than K_t.
rows.statement: Flags Guna as still operationally undefined -- five candidate mathematical meanings for Mode(K_t) (epistemic regime, transformation regime, uncertainty regime, decision bias, stability regime) with no measurable criteria chosen, warning it remains 'purely metaphorical' otherwise. Separately flags time t itself as underdefined among six candidates (wall-clock, observation sequence, version, event number, knowledge revision, logical time), suggesting KnowledgeOS may need event/logical time (notated K^(n)) rather than a single physical time index K_t.
missing: measurable Guna criteria
choice of time semantics

rows.anchor: Instead of pretending G_t are literal mathematical quantities, define them as operational regimes. Mode(K_t)=Sattva might correspond to: high consistency, high evidence quality, low unnecessary transformation, stable state, low contradiction. Rajas/Tamas would need their own measurable characteristics. If this cannot be done rigorously, Guṇa should remain a philosophical lens rather than a Kernel primitive. That distinction is essential.
rows.statement: Proposes defining Guna modes as measurable operational regimes rather than literal quantities, giving a candidate five-property characterization of Sattva (high consistency, high evidence quality, low unnecessary transformation, stable state, low contradiction) with Rajas/Tamas needing their own measurable characteristics -- explicitly conditioning Guna's kernel-primitive status on whether this rigorous characterization succeeds; if not, it must remain a philosophical lens only.

sources.note: Step 260's final, most rigorous formalization of KnowledgeOS state minimality as a behavioral-equivalence quotient K*=H/equiv_T, separating Existence/Uniqueness(up to isomorphism)/Representability/Computability/Decidability/Composability as independent unproven properties; concludes the long-discussed K=(K,C,T,E,A) tuple remains CANDIDATE not THEORY since the defining biconditional (the 'minimality sandwich') was never proven for it; sets up Step 261's Equality/Identity resolution as the next unavoidable dependency.

rows.anchor: We must not define K* as: the tuple with the fewest fields. That would be an engineering compression criterion, not a semantic minimality criterion. ... Semantic minimality != syntactic compactness.
rows.statement: Restates and sharpens the field-count-is-not-minimality principle with a worked example (a 4-field K1 vs a 2-field K2 -- fewer fields does not make K2 more minimal), concluding semantic minimality is categorically distinct from syntactic compactness.

rows.anchor: H1 equiv H2 iff forall O in O: O(H1)=O(H2), subject to the exact domain and observation semantics eventually established for KnowledgeOS. This is the behavioral foundation of minimality.
rows.statement: Defines observational distinguishability as the behavioral foundation of minimality: two histories are equivalent iff every permitted observation/operation agrees on them.

rows.anchor: H1 equiv_T H2 iff forall T in T: T(H1) equiv_T T(H2) [potentially recursive, cannot simply declare it correct] ... we therefore need to distinguish: Candidate definition equiv_T^cand from Proven behavioral equivalence equiv_T^prov. At this stage we have the former.
rows.statement: Flags the natural recursive-looking definition of transformation-relative equivalence as needing careful treatment (it cannot simply be declared correct), distinguishing a candidate definition from a proven behavioral equivalence -- only the former exists at this stage.

rows.anchor: Reflexivity: PROVISIONALLY DERIVED, not yet universally proven ... if an observation is stochastic, nondeterministic, or dependent on an unmodeled environment, then this needs qualification. Symmetry: DERIVED under ordinary observation equality. Transitivity: DERIVED under ordinary equality. ... thi
rows.statement: Proves the 3 standard equivalence-relation properties for the candidate observational equivalence: reflexivity only provisionally (fails to be automatic if observations are stochastic/nondeterministic/environment-dependent), symmetry and transitivity both derived under ordinary equality -- all three still depend on the eventual full closure and definition of the permitted-observation set O.

rows.anchor: equiv must be a congruence for T. This links Step 260 directly to Step 259. The minimal state is therefore not merely H/equiv for any equivalence relation. It must be a quotient under an equivalence relation that respects the transformation algebra.
rows.statement: Adds the congruence requirement on top of mere equivalence-relation status: being reflexive/symmetric/transitive is not sufficient for a quotient to be a valid state abstraction -- the equivalence must additionally be preserved by every transformation, directly linking back to Step 248/255's congruence criterion.

rows.anchor: K* = H / equiv_T where [H] = {H' in H | H' equiv_T H}. The candidate state is therefore an equivalence class of histories. A Knowledge State need not be the history itself; it can be the semantic information that distinguishes one behavioral class of histories from another.
rows.statement: States the candidate quotient construction K*=H/equiv_T (equivalence classes of histories under the congruence-respecting relation) as conceptually powerful precisely because a Knowledge State need not literally be the history, only the semantic information distinguishing behavioral classes -- the final, most rigorous form of Step 247's (S1609) equivalence-class hypothesis.

rows.anchor: Mathematically H/equiv may exist as a set. But that does not mean KnowledgeOS can compute [H]. Nor does it mean that an implementation can store a canonical representative. Existence != Representability != Computability.
rows.statement: States the critical 3-way separation of Existence, Representability, and Computability for the quotient construction -- a set can exist mathematically without an implementation being able to compute or store a canonical representative of it, and these three properties must each be investigated independently.

rows.anchor: Existence: CANDIDATE, because the complete history domain and complete mandatory operation/observation family are not yet formally closed.
rows.statement: Rates the quotient's mathematical existence as merely CANDIDATE status, since neither the full history domain nor the complete mandatory operation/observation family has been formally closed yet.

rows.anchor: K1=(content,status) and K2=(encoded_content,status_code) ... may have different representations but the same semantics. Therefore the representation of K* need not be unique. What may be unique is the quotient up to isomorphism. Unique representation vs Unique semantic quotient up to isomorphism.
rows.statement: Distinguishes unique representation from unique-up-to-isomorphism semantic quotient, using a worked example of two structurally different but semantically equivalent representations -- the latter (uniqueness up to isomorphism) is the only mathematically meaningful uniqueness target.

rows.anchor: If no such representation is available under the required constraints, then the mathematical theory may exist but fail computationally. This is not a contradiction. It would be: Mathematically valid, computationally unusable.
rows.statement: Names the specific, non-contradictory failure mode of a mathematically valid but computationally unusable theory: a quotient can exist abstractly with no effective encode/decode mapping to a finite representation available under KnowledgeOS's actual constraints.

rows.anchor: for arbitrary histories and arbitrarily rich semantic transformations, this cannot be assumed. Decidability of KnowledgeOS semantic equivalence = UNRESOLVED. This is a serious gate.
rows.statement: Names decidability of the semantic-equivalence test itself as UNRESOLVED and a serious gate: no algorithm is shown to terminate and correctly decide H1 equiv H2 for arbitrary histories under arbitrarily rich transformations.

rows.anchor: If equivalence is undecidable, quotient membership may also be undecidable. Membership depends directly on equality/equivalence. ... Hash identity != semantic identity unless explicitly defined and justified. This issue must be resolved in Step 261.
rows.statement: Shows Membership inherits any undecidability of the underlying equivalence test, and separately warns a collision-resistant hash of an equivalence class is neither automatically semantic identity nor a mathematical proof of equality (nor does distinct hashing disprove semantic sameness) unless explicitly justified -- deferring full resolution to Step 261.

rows.anchor: For a composition operation Merge(K1,K2) to be well-defined, the result must be independent of representatives. ... This is exactly another congruence requirement. Composability is not automatic from quotient existence. ... If Merge(H1,H2) not-equiv Merge(H1',H2'), then Merge does not descend to the
rows.statement: Proves Composability of Merge over the quotient is a distinct congruence requirement (representative-independence: equivalent inputs must produce equivalent Merge outputs), not automatic from mere quotient existence; if it fails, Merge simply does not descend to a well-defined K* x K* -> K* operation, requiring one of 5 named remedies (a richer K, additional external context, a restricted Merge domain, a partial operation, or a different semantic interpretation).

rows.anchor: A minimal abstraction should identify all histories that are behaviorally indistinguishable. F* should be the coarsest sufficient abstraction. ... Too coarse: F loses required information. Too fine: F retains unnecessary distinctions. Minimal: F(H1)=F(H2) iff H1 equiv H2.
rows.statement: Gives the final precise 3-way classification of a candidate state abstraction (too coarse: loses required information; too fine: retains unnecessary distinctions; minimal: the biconditional F(H1)=F(H2) iff H1 equiv H2 holds exactly), extending Step 255's coarsest-abstraction target into a complete taxonomy.

rows.anchor: Sufficiency: F(H1)=F(H2) => H1 equiv H2. Completeness of abstraction: H1 equiv H2 => F(H1)=F(H2). Together: the minimality sandwich. If achieved, F is a canonical representation of the behavioral quotient.
rows.statement: Names the 'minimality sandwich': the two directional implications (sufficiency and completeness-of-abstraction) whose conjunction is exactly the target biconditional defining a canonical representation of the behavioral quotient.

rows.anchor: The previously discussed K=(K,C,T,E,A) cannot yet be accepted as K*. Why? Because no proof has established F(H1)=F(H2) iff H1 equiv H2. Therefore the tuple remains CANDIDATE rather than THEORY.
rows.statement: Applies the minimality-sandwich criterion directly to the long-discussed 5-tuple K=(K,C,T,E,A), finding the required biconditional has never been proven for it, so it remains a CANDIDATE, not a THEORY -- consistent with the mandate's instruction not to select a kernel merely for being later or more elegant.

rows.anchor: 13-component removal test table: Content Necessary-strongly-supported; Identity Likely-necessary-formal-test-required; [11 further components: Epistemic status, Evidence, Provenance, Temporal validity, Context, Contradiction, Uncertainty, Lineage, Full history, Policy, Authority] all Unresolved. The
rows.statement: Runs the removal test on 13 candidate K-components, finding only Content strongly supported as necessary and Identity likely necessary, with the remaining 11 (epistemic status, evidence, provenance, temporal validity, context, contradiction, uncertainty, lineage, full history, policy, authority) all explicitly and deliberately left Unresolved rather than guessed at.

rows.anchor: A particularly important failure would be: not-exists K within the proposed state-only representation class such that all mandatory transformations are well-defined. That would mean KnowledgeOS requires History or ExternalContext or TypedFamily rather than one closed state. This would not mean the t
rows.statement: States that the strongest possible negative result (no sufficient state-only K exists at all, so History/ExternalContext/TypedFamily is structurally required) would be a successful research outcome under the governing methodology, not a theory failure -- it would falsify the one-state-kernel hypothesis specifically, one of (at least) 3 legitimate possible outcomes of the removal analysis (the others being a non-tuple K* with typed external interfaces, or a typed family of states).

rows.anchor: Mathematical completeness: YELLOW -- candidate equivalence and quotient construction are defined, but the complete operation family and semantic domain are not closed. Computational completeness: RED -- no executable quotient/equality algorithm has yet been demonstrated. Engineering completeness: RE
rows.statement: Reports the mandated 3-dimension completeness scorecard as YELLOW (mathematical, partial), RED (computational, no executable algorithm), RED (engineering, no implementation correspondence), explicitly kept as 3 separate statuses rather than collapsed into one overall verdict.

rows.anchor: K* is not 'the smallest tuple'. Instead: K* = a representation of the coarsest behavioral equivalence classes of admissible histories such that every mandatory operation is well-defined on those classes. Equivalently K* approx H/equiv_T provided the quotient construction survives the existence, cong
rows.statement: States the step's central sharpened definition of the desired KnowledgeOS kernel: not the smallest tuple, but a representation of the coarsest behavioral equivalence classes on which every mandatory operation is well-defined, approximately H/equiv_T conditional on surviving all the named formal tests (existence, congruence, representability, computability).

rows.anchor: We cannot determine whether two quotient states are the same until equality is defined. ... Step 261 must therefore formally resolve K1=K2 and a in K. It must distinguish semantic equality, structural equality, identity, observational equivalence, historical equality, provenance equality and test th
rows.statement: Sets Step 261 (Equality and Identity) as unavoidable, since minimality analysis exposed that quotient-state sameness cannot be determined without a prior resolved equality definition; requires distinguishing 6 named equality notions and testing each against 7 named operations, with an explicit ban on proceeding to final kernel selection while equality remains ambiguous.

lineage_claims.quote: Step 261 -- Equality and Identity ... So the next step is Step 261, not another candidate-kernel proposal.

lexical.anchor: We must not define K* as: the tuple with the fewest fields. That would be an engineering compression criterion, not a semantic minimality criterion. ... Semantic minimality != syntactic compactness.

formal.anchor: K* = H / equiv_T where [H] = {H' in H | H' equiv_T H}. The candidate state is therefore an equivalence class of histories. A Knowledge State need not be the history itself; it can be the semantic information that distinguishes one behavioral class of histories from another.

sources.note: A structured 15-document (Document 00 through 14) KnowledgeOS Theory v1.2 write-up dated 2026-09-04, organizationally distinct from the earlier 50-section consolidated draft (knowledgeos-information-transformation-theory-consolidated-draft-2026-09) though covering overlapping Zero/adequacy/realization/representation-reduction ground -- flagged POSSIBLY the same underlying theory-writing effort pending confirmation. This batch (B0065) contributes four of the fifteen: Document 03a (the concept of Zero -- distinguishes Zero from sufficiency/adequacy, from invariance, from graphoid-style conditional-irrelevance (fails both composition and decomposition), and from an independence system/matroid; states the exact Remainder identity A==C in 1182/1182 cases with B a different object; documents the elimination process L as terminating but non-confluent; and records higher-order eliminability up to k=3 for n<=6); Document 05 (Realization vs Adequacy formally separated, but the separation was never experimentally exhibited -- a named design defect in KR-REP-REDUCTION -- with one open conjecture Realization=>Adequacy); Document 06 (the R5->R4 rounding-to-3-significant-figures representation-adequacy boundary, explicitly scope-bound to one carrier/inquiry/chain/contract; Zero does NOT mark the boundary; a prior rank-convention/DECISION-01 claim is explicitly withdrawn after the audit found rank conventions are not invertible under ties); and Document 12 (a DDD strategic architecture model over the Zero/adequacy/realization kernel research -- five candidate bounded contexts, a constitutional read-disjointness invariant no single context can own, an Evidence & Contradiction context with unresolved ownership blocked on DECISION-02, aggregate/event/port design forced by the data, and eight named anti-patterns).

rows.anchor: This document models; it decides nothing. ... the standing rule is: resolve ownership of every invariant BEFORE protecting it.
rows.statement: States the document's own status (`[DESIGN]`, kernel NOT SELECTED) and the governing rule that ownership of every invariant must be resolved before any tactical protection of it is designed.

rows.anchor: Read-disjointness is a constitutional invariant. No context owns it. Every context preserves it. ... its provenance map is what makes the invariant checkable.
rows.statement: Argues read-disjointness (relating Pi, Q, T simultaneously) cannot be owned by Inquiry, Eliminability or Transformation individually, and must instead be a shared constitutional invariant every bounded context preserves, echoing the anonymity-invariant shape found in a sibling platform.

rows.anchor: Evidence & Contradiction has unresolved ownership because DECISION-02 -- is phi a semantic evaluation frame or an evidence partition? -- is open. The model must not proceed to tactical work there.
rows.statement: Explicitly leaves the Evidence & Contradiction bounded context's ownership unresolved pending an open governance decision, refusing to proceed to tactical modelling there.

rows.anchor: EliminationAssessment must carry its contract and reference. Zero is contract-relative (495/4049 verdicts flip) and reference-relative (541/4260). ... There is no EliminableCore aggregate.
rows.statement: Derives two aggregate-boundary design rules directly from prior experimental numbers: a stored Zero verdict must carry its full (contract, reference) index or it is not a fact when reused, and no 'EliminableCore' aggregate may cache minimal eliminable sets and close upward since Z is not generated by its minimal elements (286/826 failures).

rows.anchor: Treating "eliminate everything eliminable" as well-defined -- L is non-confluent; the normal form depends on order. ... Letting a ticket accrete into architecture -- architecture produces tickets; tickets do not become architecture.
rows.statement: Lists eight named anti-patterns each traced to a specific earlier experimental finding, including treating full elimination as well-defined, a single scalar 'reduction size', re-fitting a decoder after seeing R, and letting tickets silently accrete into architecture.

rows.anchor: Zero is the question "can this be removed without changing what I have chosen to observe?" -- and every word of that sentence is load-bearing.
rows.statement: Gives the canonical one-sentence definition of Zero_{T,Pi}(S;D) with a word-by-word table (this/removed/changing/I have chosen/observe) explaining exactly what each word forces, distinguishing 'the change is zero' from 'a thing being empty or worthless'.

rows.anchor: Zero is not sufficiency -- adequacy is. ... Sufficiency is about what a representation retains. Zero is about what a case can lose.
rows.statement: Distinguishes Zero from sufficiency/adequacy (built read-disjoint and measured independent per document 07) so a design reaching for Zero when it wants sufficiency will delete the wrong things.

rows.anchor: Zero fails in both directions between the element level and the set level. It is therefore not an irrelevance relation in the graphoid sense ... [x,x] ... redundancy ... [+c,-c] ... emergent eliminability
rows.statement: States that Zero fails both graphoid-axiom directions (composition: 131 violations; decomposition: 63 violations), with the two canonical counterexample shapes named as the whole concept: [x,x] (redundancy, a composition failure) and [+c,-c] (emergent eliminability under a cancelling contract, a decomposition failure).

rows.anchor: A - Eliminated \equiv C in 1182/1182 -- exactly ... B is a different object. The transformation residual is not what the contract leaves unresolved.
rows.statement: States the Remainder trichotomy's exact positive identity: 'not eliminated' equals exactly 'contract-relevant unresolved material' without exception in 1182/1182 tested cases, while the transformation residual (B) is a genuinely different object, separating the residue of the operation from the residue of the concern.

rows.anchor: One elimination in six is blocked by boundary information alone ... the rule-based and counterfactual notions of eliminability agree only 55.75% of the time ... 1559 elements the rule would remove are not Zero, against 301 that are Zero but the rule keeps.
rows.statement: Reports the asymmetric-bias finding as a concept-level warning: a rule-over-field-types eliminability heuristic is wrong far more often in the dangerous over-elimination direction than the safe direction, so eliminability must never be implemented as such a rule.

rows.anchor: L is not a projection and not an interior operator. It is a terminating, non-confluent rewriting process. ... Which normal form you reach depends on the order you eliminate in.
rows.statement: Establishes that repeated-elimination L is reductive, terminating and iteration-monotone-decreasing but non-confluent (11/1162 non-commuting) and only operator-relative idempotent; concludes 'eliminate everything eliminable' names no unique object unless an order is fixed and declared.

rows.anchor: Is there a well-defined group/set formulation of Zero? OPEN -- H5+H6 show the element-wise formulation fails in both directions; they do not supply the replacement. This is the deepest open question about the concept.
rows.statement: Names the deepest unresolved question about the Zero concept: no replacement group/set formulation exists even though the element-wise one is refuted in both directions; also leaves L's monotonicity, k>3 higher-order eliminability, and semantic equivalence explicitly open.

rows.anchor: A representation R=T(D) realizes Q under decoder O iff O(R)=Q(D). ... O is fixed in advance, as part of the inquiry frame. ... If O may be chosen after seeing R, then "realization" is just adequacy restated.
rows.statement: Defines Realization with the decoder O fixed in advance as part of the inquiry frame, stating that fixing is the entire content of the definition -- a claim about the decoder you actually have, not the existence of one.

rows.anchor: Adequate \land \neg C(R) \Rightarrow not realizable, though the information is present. ... This is why C belongs in the frame and not in the transformation.
rows.statement: Distinguishes Adequacy (does R determine Q, an existential/population-level question) from Realization (does this fixed decoder recover Q, a per-case question), showing they diverge for two independent reasons: a weaker-than-needed decoder, or a failing use-time constraint C.

rows.anchor: KR-REP-REDUCTION's design failed to operationalize the adequacy/realization separation. ... the only adequate level, R5, has F=1.0000. ... this experiment could not exhibit it, and no experiment yet has.
rows.statement: Names a specific design defect: the chain's transformations never dropped a record so C could never fail, and the decoder was strong enough at the one adequate level, so the experiment excluded its own target case by construction -- the separation is real by definition but was never exhibited.

rows.anchor: Realization \Rightarrow Adequacy. ... What would refute it: a case set on which O(T(D))=Q(D) holds throughout while the fiber is Q-heterogeneous ... Not tested.
rows.statement: States the one open conjecture in the document with an explicit refutation condition (a decoder right by luck on observed cases without being determined by R), noting the converse (Adequacy=>Realization) is already refuted.

rows.anchor: Last adequate stage: R5. First inadequate: R4. Crossing transformation: T4 -- rounding to 3 significant digits. ... TEST reproduces TRAIN closely
rows.statement: Reports the located adequacy boundary (R5 adequate at Hhat=0, R4 inadequate at Hhat=0.4299) reproduced closely on an independent test split (0.4408 vs 0.4299), confirming it is not a one-sample artifact.

rows.anchor: We may NOT say: "Three significant digits is the universal preservation limit." We may say: for this carrier, this inquiry Q, this transformation chain, this contract and this value domain, rounding ... crossed the observed preservation boundary.
rows.statement: States the scope-bound discipline the whole result exists to teach: the boundary is a property of the inquiry frame (carrier, Q, chain, contract, value domain), not a universal numeric limit; by the DPI corollary the boundary is unique and cannot be re-crossed back into adequacy along the sequential chain.

rows.anchor: The Zero rate at the boundary crossing is not distinguishable from the rate at a non-crossing step, and is in fact lower. Eliminability carries no signal about where preservation fails.
rows.statement: Reports the direct test of hypothesis H-RR2 (Zero marks the adequacy boundary): refuted -- the Zero rate at the actual boundary crossing (0.0377) is not higher than, and is in fact lower than, the rate at a non-crossing step (0.0426).

rows.anchor: Rank conventions are NOT invertible. desc \neq (n+1) - asc when values tie -- 21369 violations ... this is NOT an instance of DECISION-01 ... The headline built on it was withdrawn -- both my wording and the review's replacement wording.
rows.statement: Records an explicit retraction: a prior claim that a rank-direction finding instantiated DECISION-01 (non-evidential invariance) required an invertible recoding between rank conventions, which the audit refuted (21,369 tie violations); both the original and the review's replacement wording are withdrawn, though the underlying adequacy/realization sensitivity gap survives as the one place that distinction was visible at all.

rows.anchor: yogartha / yogarudhartha / rudhartha = intrinsic / contextual / conventional meaning; word frequency != meaning
rows.statement: The three-layer semantic model, named the strongest contribution of the Sanskrit-grammar lens: an anti-collapse lesson directly targeting LLM word-frequency-as-meaning failures.

rows.anchor: semantic sandhi: context compatibility rules, meaning alignment rules, conflict resolution rules (A+B transform by rules at the boundary, never simple concatenation)
rows.statement: A knowledge-composition mechanism analogous to Sanskrit's sound-combination rules, proposed to feed the typed epistemic graph's composition rules and the Verification Gate.

rows.anchor: transformation history as a first-class knowledge-object structure: origin + transformation rule + new expression + semantic continuity
rows.statement: The concrete storage shape for the Escher invariant-preserving-transformation target, derived from the dhatu-root-to-derived-word lineage pattern.

rows.anchor: the eight-case epistemic grammar (Who? Does what? Using what? For whom? From where? Belongs to whom? In which context?) as a relationship ontology
rows.statement: Proposes Sanskrit's grammatical case system as a richer relationship vocabulary for the typed epistemic graph than a bare node-edge label set.

rows.anchor: guna/vrddhi maturation ladder: Observation -> Information -> Knowledge -> Understanding -> Wisdom; growth != replacement
rows.statement: Maps Sanskrit's controlled-amplification vowel transformations to a knowledge-maturity ladder where growth preserves identity while raising expression level.

rows.anchor: refinement: not 'word order does not matter' but 'meaning should be reconstructed from invariant relationships'
rows.statement: The HPA explicitly corrects the folk claim about Sanskrit word-order freedom before drawing the architectural lesson, modeling a discipline of not overclaiming from a linguistic fact.

rows.anchor: KnowledgeOS is not a language model; it is a meaning-preservation and meaning-transformation system.
rows.statement: A re-derivation of the admitted character stance from the fifth (linguistic/grammatical) derivation route, contrasting LLM's Expression->Probability->Expression with KnowledgeOS's Meaning Root->Context->Evidence->Reasoning Rules->Expression.

rows.anchor: Pāṇini's Aṣṭādhyāyī is a 2,500-year-old precedent for computational semantic representation that is order-independent and relationship-first (deterministic production rules, recursive application, precedence-based conflict resolution, meta-linguistic notation).
rows.statement: External-research finding (citing linguistics/CS literature) offered as strong evidence that Karaka-based, permutation-invariant semantic representation is not a novel invention but has a long computational-linguistics precedent (PERIN, 2020 CoNLL shared-task winner).

rows.anchor: Karaka theory: eight semantic roles (Karta/Karma/Karana/Sampradana/Apadana/Adhikarana/Sambandha/Sambodhana) mapped to Actor/Object/Instrument/Beneficiary/Source/Context/Relationship/Address
rows.statement: A concrete semantic-role-labeling scheme proposed as a strong candidate mechanism (ARTHA-MECH-001), citing real Sanskrit-NLP literature.

rows.anchor: case-to-relationship mapping table (nominative=Who/what asserts?; accusative=What is affected?; instrumental=Through what evidence/tool?; dative=For whom/purpose?; ablative=From where/source?; genitive=Ownership/provenance; locative=Context; vocative=Intended recipient)
rows.statement: The original (v1) worked mapping of the eight Sanskrit grammatical cases onto knowledge-relationship roles, later reused verbatim in the v2 deepening and the formal reviews.

rows.anchor: Sanskrit Grammar Lens = Semantic Integrity & Transformation Lens; among all lenses so far, Sanskrit grammar is one of the closest analogues to the internal language of KnowledgeOS itself.
rows.statement: The author's own closing classification, later quoted verbatim in the formal review (S0290).

rows.anchor: Human expression -> Lexical recognition -> Candidate interpretations -> Contextual/governance interpretation -> Canonical domain act -> Deterministic execution ... The Kernel should consume an already-resolved domain candidate; it should not solve linguistic ambiguity.
rows.statement: Sanskrit/compiler lens critique offers a compiler-analogy pipeline (human expression -> lexical recognition -> candidate interpretations -> contextual/governance interpretation -> canonical domain act -> deterministic execution) mapped to front-end (interpretation) / semantic boundary (meaning candidate) / domain core (constitutionally valid transition) / runtime layer (execution), yielding the principle that the Kernel consumes an already-resolved domain candidate and does not itself resolve linguistic ambiguity -- offered as possibly a better model than 'Kernel = admission boundary' alone.

rows.anchor: Candidate interpretation != Knowledge. ... CandidateKnowledge + EvidenceReferences + Justification + Context -> Kernel domain decision ... not: raw expression -> Kernel -> meaning
rows.statement: Extends the Sanskrit-compiler 'Expression != Meaning' lens to 'Candidate interpretation != Knowledge', concluding the Kernel should not care how a candidate was produced and its input should be a structured CandidateKnowledge+EvidenceReferences+Justification+Context bundle, never raw expression -- preserving the existing Expression<->Meaning boundary and P5's finding that semantic mechanisms remain replaceable providers.

rows.anchor: 4. Paninian / Sanskrit Grammar Lens -- Generate Structure from Rules ... Can expression be transformed deterministically into structured representation through explicit rules? ... A deterministic semantic compiler can exist outside the Kernel.
rows.statement: Defines the Paninian/Sanskrit-grammar lens (distinct from Vani: can expression be transformed deterministically into structured representation via explicit rules -- Expression -> morphological/syntactic analysis -> semantic roles -> structured candidate), concluding the architectural lesson is not to build Sanskrit into the Kernel but that a deterministic semantic compiler may exist outside it.

rows.anchor: Don't interpret a token in isolation. Determine its role and relationship within the whole expression. ... Sanskrit cases encode relations such as actor, object, means, source, ownership and context. ... EVENT: Approval. ACTOR: Architect. OBJECT: Nexus Upgrade. BASIS/INSTRUMENT: Security Assessment.
rows.statement: Borrows from Sanskrit case grammar the principle 'don't interpret a token in isolation, determine its role and relationship within the whole expression' -- Sanskrit cases encode relations like actor, object, means, source, ownership, context. Worked example: 'The architect approved the Nexus upgrade based on the security assessment' parses (unlike a flat tokenizer) into EVENT=Approval, ACTOR=Architect, OBJECT=Nexus Upgrade, BASIS/INSTRUMENT=Security Assessment.
invariants: a token is never interpreted without its relational role in the full expression

rows.anchor: we should NOT copy Sanskrit grammar literally. ... it proposes extracting architectural principles such as: root-based semantics; explicit relationships; generative transformation rules; separation of meaning and expression. ... our architecture should not be: KnowledgeOS -> Sanskrit grammar. It should be: Sanskrit grammar -> architectural lens -> semantic parsing principles -> KnowledgeOS semantic compiler.
rows.statement: Explicit warning against literally adopting Sanskrit grammar into KnowledgeOS: the value is in extracted architectural principles (root-based semantics, explicit relationships, generative transformation rules, separation of meaning and expression), never the grammar itself as an implementation. The correct chain is Sanskrit grammar -> architectural lens -> semantic parsing principles -> KnowledgeOS semantic compiler, never a direct KnowledgeOS -> Sanskrit grammar dependency.
invariants: KnowledgeOS never directly depends on Sanskrit grammar -- only on architectural principles distilled from it

rows.anchor: Expression != Meaning ... the uploaded research explicitly identifies this as a central principle. ... we need a transformation: Expression -> MeaningStructure and only then: MeaningStructure -> Dimensions + Values + Relations. ... Expression -- semantic rules --> State structure and later: State structure -- expression rules --> Expression.
rows.statement: Identifies the single most valuable Sanskrit-derived idea as Expression != Meaning, requiring a two-stage transformation Expression -> MeaningStructure -> Dimensions+Values+Relations; inverting the Paninian rule-based-transformation analogy gives a bidirectional pair: Expression --semantic rules--> State structure, and State structure --expression rules--> Expression.
invariants: expression and meaning are never identified with each other

rows.anchor: Sanskrit grammar can help us determine: What role does this expression play? It cannot by itself determine: Whether the statement is true. ... Semantic parsing != Epistemic validation. This distinction is critical.
rows.statement: States a critical limit of the grammar lens: it can determine what role an expression plays (grammar can parse 'Nexus runs version 3.85' perfectly) but cannot by itself determine whether the statement is true -- truth still requires Evidence->Source->Observation->Validation->Truth/uncertainty. Formalizes Semantic parsing != Epistemic validation as a critical, never-to-be-conflated distinction.
invariants: successfully parsing an expression's semantic structure never by itself establishes the truth of the claim

sources.note: Explicit epistemic rule adopted within Step 285: a philosophical (Gita) correspondence may generate a hypothesis, expose a modelling distinction, suggest an analogy, or challenge an assumption, but may NOT by itself establish a mathematical axiom, prove an invariant, select canonical K, select an operation, or establish a governance rule; every Gita->KnowledgeOS mapping must be classified as one of ANALOGY, HEURISTIC, DESIGN HYPOTHESIS, FORMAL DERIVATION, or GOVERNANCE DECISION, and only the last two can establish normative semantics.

rows.anchor: I would write Step 285 as a formal research step, not as a philosophical essay. The Gita should provide a conceptual lens and design hypothesis, while the mathematical/DDD work determines what can actually enter KnowledgeOS theory. In particular, we should not treat Gita concepts as axioms unless the derivation explicitly justifies that move.
rows.statement: Opening methodological ruling establishing that Step 285 is a formal research artifact, not philosophical prose, and that the Bhagavad Gita may only supply a conceptual lens/design hypothesis — mathematics and DDD derivation alone determine canonical KnowledgeOS content; explicitly bars treating Gita concepts as axioms absent justified derivation.

rows.anchor: Gita insight ≠ KnowledgeOS theorem ... A philosophical correspondence may: generate a hypothesis; expose a modelling distinction; suggest a useful analogy; challenge an implicit assumption. It may not, by itself: establish a mathematical axiom; prove an invariant; select the canonical K; select an operation; establish a governance rule. ... ANALOGY / HEURISTIC / DESIGN HYPOTHESIS / FORMAL DERIVATION / GOVERNANCE DECISION. Only the final two can establish normative KnowledgeOS semantics.

sources.note: Gap-discovery comparison of KnowledgeOS's RevisionType taxonomy against AGM belief revision, Katsuno-Mendelzon (KM) update, Hansson base revision, non-prioritized/credibility-limited revision, and Doyle's JTMS: finds FOUR exact correspondences (RevisionType::Evolution cong KM update; RevisionType::Correction/Refutation cong AGM revision; governed admission cong credibility-limited revision with credibility set C = Policy x Authority; Revision=EventAddition+StateReDerivation cong a JTMS, since the corpus's own Fagin extraction already states 'knowledge history is monotonic in preservation; knowledge state is not necessarily monotonic in projection' -- exactly the JTMS invariant) -- more exact correspondences than any other theory in this comparison series -- while finding the corpus's assertion set A is a Hansson belief BASE (not an AGM belief set K=Cn(K), measured 0 occurrences of a consequence operator), that AGM's Success postulate fails for governed admission (a proposal may be rejected), that Sigma (the Supported/Refuted status pair, isomorphic to {0,1}^2) is a PRODUCT not a total entrenchment ORDER so cannot be an entrenchment ordering, and -- its most striking finding -- that the corpus's Reinterpretation and ModelRevision revision types are changes to the INTERPRETATION FUNCTION which AGM cannot express at all (AGM holds the language L and its interpretation fixed), framed as the corpus formalizing something AGM chose to hold constant rather than being under-formalized on that axis. Verdict: 'THE CLOSEST OF THE FIVE -- and the corpus is ahead of the framework on one axis', with six falsifiable hypotheses BR-H1..BR-H6.

rows.anchor: Evolution <-> KM update; Correction/Refutation <-> AGM revision. This is a genuine result and the corpus does not know it.
rows.statement: Finds RevisionType::Evolution (the corpus's 'the system really changed from 3.69 to 3.70', boxed 'Evolution is not an error') is exactly Katsuno-Mendelzon's motivating case for UPDATE (the world changed, the old belief was correct then), while Correction/Refutation match AGM REVISION (new information about a static world); notes AGM is mentioned only 5 times across 564 corpus files and the KM revision/update distinction appears nowhere, so the corpus independently re-derived, from a version-number example, a distinction belief-revision literature has held since 1991 -- and split it six ways where KM splits two.

rows.anchor: The credibility set C is exactly Policy x Authority. ... C gates input acceptance; Policy+Authority gate admission; both leave the prior state unchanged on rejection.
rows.statement: Finds the corpus's governed admission (Closure-03: LLM proposes, Lord evaluates, Governance authorizes; a proposal may be rejected) is exactly credibility-limited (non-prioritized) revision K⊛phi = K*phi if phi in C, else K, with the credibility set C identified structure-preservingly as Policy x Authority.

rows.anchor: H monotone AND K'=Derive(H') non-monotone === JTMS
rows.statement: Finds the corpus's boxed Revision = EventAddition + StateReDerivation (H'=H union {E_revision}, K'=Derive(H',Omega,EC,M)) is exactly a Doyle-style JTMS: the corpus's own Fagin extraction already states 'knowledge history is monotonic in preservation; knowledge state is not necessarily monotonic in projection', which is the JTMS invariant verbatim (justification store grows monotonically, derived belief set is non-monotone).

rows.anchor: AGM does not apply to A as stated. Hansson's base revision does. ... importing AGM results would import theorems that are false of A.
rows.statement: Structural incompatibility: AGM's carrier K=Cn(K) is deductively closed, but the corpus's assertion set A (measured: zero occurrences of a consequence operator Cn) is a finite set of asserted items with identity/provenance/evidence links, i.e. a Hansson belief BASE, not a belief SET; since base contraction and AGM contraction on Cn(B) are provably inequivalent, naively importing AGM theorems would import claims false of A.

rows.anchor: Two of the corpus's six revision types are changes to the interpretation function, which AGM cannot express. ... This is the largest single gap found in this document, and it runs against the external theory rather than against KnowledgeOS.
rows.statement: Decisive finding: AGM holds the language L and its interpretation fixed -- every operator maps L-sentences to L-sentences, with no operator for changing what sentences MEAN -- but the corpus's Reinterpretation ('the original observation was valid, but we interpreted it incorrectly', a change in Evidence(O,P,C,R)'s rule R) and ModelRevision ('reasonable under the old model, but the model itself was subsequently changed', a change in M within Derive(H,Omega,EC,M)) are both first-class corpus revision types with no AGM counterpart at all; framed as the corpus formalizing something AGM chose to hold constant, i.e. the gap runs against the external theory, not against KnowledgeOS.

rows.anchor: Sigma cong {0,1}^2 is a product, not an order. Supported (1,0) and Refuted (0,1) are incomparable ... Sigma cannot be an entrenchment ordering.
rows.statement: Refutes mapping Sigma onto an AGM entrenchment ordering: AGM entrenchment <= is a total, transitive preorder satisfying dominance and minimality, but the corpus's Sigma (isomorphic to {0,1}^2, the Supported/Refuted product) is a product structure, not an order -- Supported(1,0) and Refuted(0,1) are incomparable, neither more entrenched than the other. Offers, only as a stated-not-adopted hypothesis (BR-H4), a lattice ordering (0,0)<={(1,0),(0,1)}<=(1,1) under set inclusion on the support set, explicitly noting this would order informativeness, not resistance-to-retraction, and the corpus asserts no such order.

rows.anchor: Retraction — "the source withdraws its support" — is not expressible in AGM, because AGM beliefs have no sources.
rows.statement: Notes AGM models a single agent's single belief set at one time with no source identifiers, while KnowledgeOS carries provenance, multiple sources, authority and an inquiry register; consequently RevisionType::Retraction (a source withdrawing its support) cannot be expressed in AGM at all and requires base revision augmented with justifications (i.e. JTMS).

rows.anchor: interpretation change | sources/provenance on beliefs | an authority predicate | a requirement set | a goal state | paraconsistent tolerance ... a consequence operator Cn | an entrenchment/plausibility order | a contraction operator
rows.statement: Lists missing primitives on the belief-revision side needed to host KnowledgeOS (interpretation change for Reinterpretation/ModelRevision; sources/provenance on beliefs for Retraction; an authority predicate for governed admission; a requirement set for Zero; a goal state for Ideal State; paraconsistent tolerance for Conflict, since AGM's K*5 Consistency postulate forbids it) and on the KnowledgeOS side needed to host belief revision (a consequence operator Cn, currently 0 occurrences, without which 'belief set' is undefined; an entrenchment/plausibility order, since nothing currently orders assertions by retractability; a contraction operator, since Retraction is named as a RevisionType but not defined as an operator, and its membership in the operator-registry O_core is unratified).

rows.anchor: BR-H1 ... BR-H2 ... BR-H3 ... BR-H4 ... BR-H5 ... BR-H6
rows.statement: States six falsifiable hypotheses with named falsifiers: BR-H1 (Evolution<->KM-update and Correction/Refutation<->AGM-revision is exact in role); BR-H2 (governed admission satisfies credibility-limited-revision postulates with C=Policy x Authority, falsified by a rejected proposal that still changes A); BR-H3 (Revision=EventAddition+StateReDerivation satisfies the JTMS invariant, falsified by a RevisionType that removes an event from H); BR-H4 (Sigma admits no total entrenchment order consistent with corpus operations); BR-H5 (Reinterpretation/ModelRevision are not definable as any AGM/KM operator composition over a fixed L); BR-H6 (because Cn is absent, no AGM theorem transfers to A unmodified, falsified by exhibiting one that holds of A for a non-trivial reason).

rows.anchor: THE CLOSEST OF THE FIVE — and the corpus is ahead of the framework on one axis ... the substrate the corpus describes is a justification store, and that is a JTMS.
rows.statement: Final verdict: belief revision is 'the closest of the five' external theories compared in this series, with four exact correspondences (more than any other), a resolvable carrier mismatch (move from AGM to base revision), and one axis (Reinterpretation/ModelRevision) where KnowledgeOS is ahead of the external framework rather than under-formalized; endorses and sharpens the corpus's own Gardenfors-derived self-description ('epistemic states and their dynamics as the primary modelling problem', Kernel=preservation substrate) into 'the substrate the corpus describes is a justification store, and that is a JTMS.'

rows.anchor: Implement Epistemic Change as multiple mechanisms ... reject a single undifferentiated K_{t+1}=delta(K_t,x). Instead ... Revision != Contraction != Update ... revision concerns correcting an epistemic state regarding a static world, whereas update concerns becoming current after the world itself changes.
rows.statement: FR-5 (section 6): rejects a single undifferentiated transition K_{t+1}=delta(K_t,x); requires distinguishing Revision(K_t,e)->K_{t+1} (correction/reorganization of a static-world epistemic state), Contraction(K_t,p)->K_{t+1} (withdrawal of a commitment), and Update(K_t,Delta W)->K_{t+1} (the represented world changed) as semantic categories (not necessarily three implementation services), following the Handbook's revision-vs-update distinction.

lineage_claims.quote: revision concerns correcting an epistemic state regarding a static world, whereas update concerns becoming current after the world itself changes

rows.anchor: Implement 'revision is constrained, not uniquely determined' ... Constraints(delta) not=> Unique(delta) ... Semantic invariants constrain admissible operations but do not, by themselves, select a unique operation unless an additional selection criterion is established. This principle applies beyond revision: equality, evaluation, contradiction, aggregation, transition, policy semantics.
rows.statement: Section 11 (general methodological principle): AGM-style material shows desirable rationality constraints do not determine a unique revision operator (Constraints(delta) does not imply Unique(delta)); generalized as 'semantic invariants constrain admissible operations but do not, by themselves, select a unique operation unless an additional selection criterion is established', explicitly extended beyond revision to equality, evaluation, contradiction, aggregation, transition, and policy semantics. Judged compatible with existing kernel discipline.
invariants: constraints do not by themselves entail a unique operation

rows.anchor: What I would NOT implement ... AGM as KnowledgeOS revision ... Event Calculus as delta ... Description Logic as KnowledgeOS ontology ... FDE as KnowledgeOS evaluation. Already experimentally rejected as sufficient ... Four-valued knowledge. Still insufficient ... Closed-world assumption. Explicitly rejected ... Query = Sat. Rejected ... TELL = requirement insertion. Rejected ... Model uniqueness = Determination. Not yet ... Distributed knowledge logic = KnowledgeOS social ontology. Not yet ... N_eff. Still off the critical path.
rows.statement: Section 18, an eleven-item explicit non-adoption list, each rejecting an over-strong external-theory identification even where the same Handbook material motivates the underlying distinction: AGM as the revision theory, Event Calculus as delta, Description Logic as ontology (subsumption/model-existence/instance-checking/open-world used only as research inputs), FDE as evaluation (already experimentally rejected), four-valued knowledge, closed-world assumption, Query=Sat, TELL=requirement-insertion, ModelUniqueness=Determination, distributed-knowledge-logic=social-ontology, and N_eff -- all explicitly rejected or deferred as established KnowledgeOS semantics.

lineage_claims.target: a hypothetical straightforward adoption of AGM/Event-Calculus/DL/FDE as KnowledgeOS semantics
lineage_claims.quote: Do not add these to KnowledgeOS Theory as established semantics

rows.anchor: Part 2: Knowledge Evolution and Change -- FR-5 Epistemic Change Typing [STRONG], FR-6 Non-Monotonic Evolution [STRONG], FR-8 Derivation Lineage [STRONG CANDIDATE]
rows.statement: Part 2 groups FR-5, FR-6 and (unusually, ahead of the Representation part) FR-8 under Knowledge Evolution and Change: FR-5 Revision != Contraction != Update, each with a distinct signature (Revision(K_t,e), Contract(K_t,p), Update(K_t,DeltaW)); FR-6 K_t not-subseteq K_{t+1} permitted, not itself indicating failure; FR-8 Support(q)={p, p->q,...} as DerivationLineage(q), status STRONG CANDIDATE pending one validation pass.

rows.anchor: Part 5: What Is NOT Implemented -- AGM as KnowledgeOS revision: Use distinctions only ... FDE as KnowledgeOS evaluation: Experimentally rejected ... N_eff: Off critical path
rows.statement: Part 5 formalizes the non-adoption list as an 11-row table (item, reason): AGM as revision (use distinctions only), Event Calculus as delta (research input only), Description Logic as ontology (research input only), FDE as evaluation (experimentally rejected), four-valued knowledge (insufficient), closed-world assumption (explicitly rejected), Query=Sat (rejected), TELL=requirement-insertion (rejected), Model-uniqueness=Determination (not yet), Distributed knowledge logic (not yet), N_eff (off critical path).

rows.anchor: Two places where KnowledgeOS exceeds the external theory: Reinterpretation and ModelRevision -- AGM/KM hold the language fixed; two of the corpus's six revision types change the interpretation function. No operator exists in the framework. Determination/Decision/Action -- a three-way split where Wald has two, and the extra cut is the one governance needs.
rows.statement: Names two places where KnowledgeOS's own formalization exceeds the compared external theory rather than merely matching or falling short of it: two of the corpus's six revision types (Reinterpretation, ModelRevision) change the interpretation function itself, something AGM/KM hold fixed and have no operator to express; and the corpus's three-way Determination/Decision/Action split adds a cut beyond Wald's two-way decision-theoretic split, specifically the cut that governance needs.
